1
李宗閔李宗閔，字損之，宗室鄭王元懿之後。 祖自仙，楚州別駕。 父，宗正卿，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使。 兄夷簡，元和中宰相。 宗閔，進士擢第，，復登制舉賢良方正科。
Li Zongmin, whose courtesy name was Sunzhi, was a descendant of Prince Yuanyi of Zheng from the imperial family. His grandfather Zixian had been vice prefect of Chuzhou. His father served as director of the Imperial Clan Court before being sent out as governor of Huazhou and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and Tongguan defense, among other posts. His elder brother Yijian had served as chief minister during the Yuanhe reign. Zongmin passed the jinshi examination and later also passed the special civil-service examination for outstanding and upright men of worth.
2
初，宗閔與牛僧孺同年登進士第，又與僧孺同年登制科。 應制之歲，李吉甫為宰相當國，宗閔、僧孺對策，指切時政之失，言甚鯁直，無所回避。 考策官楊於陵、韋貫之、李益等又第其策為中等，又為不中第者註解牛、李策語，同為唱誹。 又言翰林學士王涯甥皇甫湜中選，考核之際，不先上言。 裴垍時為學士，居中覆視，無所異同。 吉甫泣訴於上前，憲宗不獲已，罷王涯、裴垍學士。 垍守戶部侍郎，涯守都官員外郎，吏部尚書楊於陵出為嶺南節度使，吏部員外郎韋貫之出為果州刺史。 王涯再貶虢州司馬，貫之再貶巴州刺史； 僧孺、宗閔亦久之不調，隨牒諸侯府。 七年，吉甫卒，方入朝為監察御史，累遷禮部員外郎。
Early on, Zongmin and Niu Sengru had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, and they also passed the special examination in the same year. In the year they took the special examination, Li Jifu was chief minister and directed the government. Zongmin and Sengru submitted their policy essays, directly criticizing the failings of current policy. Their language was blunt and unyielding, and they held nothing back. The examiners Yang Yuling, Wei Guanzhi, Li Yi, and others also ranked their essays in the middle tier. They further annotated Niu and Li's policy essays for those who had failed the examination, joining together in mutual mockery. They also charged that Huangfu Shi, nephew of Hanlin academician Wang Ya, had been selected, and that during the evaluation the examiners had not first reported this to the throne. Pei Ji was then a Hanlin academician and reviewed the papers from within the palace, finding nothing out of order. Jifu wept and complained before the emperor. Emperor Xianzong, unable to do otherwise, removed Wang Ya and Pei Ji from their Hanlin posts. Ji retained his post as vice minister of revenue; Ya retained his post as vice director in the Ministry of Justice; Minister of Personnel Yang Yuling was sent out as military governor of Lingnan; and Vice Director of Personnel Wei Guanzhi was sent out as prefect of Guo. Wang Ya was demoted again to assistant administrator of Guo Prefecture, and Guanzhi was demoted again to prefect of Ba. Sengru and Zongmin also went long without regular appointment and took staff positions in various regional administrations. In the seventh year, after Jifu died, Zongmin finally entered court as a supervisory censor and was promoted in succession to vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
3
，宰相裴度出征吳元濟，奏宗閔為彰義軍觀察判官。 賊平，遷駕部郎中，又以本官知制誥。 穆宗即位，拜中書舍人。 時自宗正卿出刺華州，父子同時承恩制，人士榮之。 ，子婿蘇巢於錢徽下進士及第，其年，巢覆落。 宗閔涉請托，貶劍州刺史。 時李吉甫子德裕為翰林學士，錢徽榜出，德裕與同職李紳、元稹連衡言於上前，雲徽受請托，所試不公，故致重覆。 比相嫌惡，因是列為朋黨，皆挾邪取權，兩相傾軋。 自是紛紜排陷，垂四十年。
When chief minister Pei Du marched against Wu Yuanji, he recommended that Zongmin serve as administrative aide to the Zhangyi observation commissioner. After the rebels were pacified, he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites for the Department of Transport and, while retaining that rank, was also put in charge of drafting imperial edicts. When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Zongmin was appointed vice director in the Secretariat. At that time his father had left the directorship of the Imperial Clan Court to serve as prefect of Huazhou, and father and son simultaneously received edicts of imperial favor—a distinction that men of standing greatly admired. His son-in-law Su Chao passed the jinshi examination under Qian Hui's examination list, but that same year Chao was struck from the rolls when the results were re-examined. Zongmin was implicated in improper solicitations and was demoted to prefect of Jian. At the time Li Jifu's son Deyu was a Hanlin academician. When Qian Hui's examination list was published, Deyu allied with his colleagues Li Shen and Yuan Zhen to speak before the emperor, charging that Hui had accepted solicitations and that the examination had been unfair, which led to the re-examination. Because the two sides came to hate each other, they were henceforth treated as rival partisan cliques, each resorting to corrupt means to seize power and striving to destroy the other. From then on, factional purges and entrapments continued for nearly forty years.
4
復入為中書舍人。 三年冬，權知禮部侍郎。 四年，貢舉事畢，權知兵部侍郎。 ，正拜兵部侍郎，父憂免。 ，起為吏部侍郎，賜金紫之服。 三年八月，以本官同平章事。
He returned to court as vice director in the Secretariat. In the winter of the third year, he served concurrently as acting vice director in the Ministry of Rites. In the fourth year, after the tribute-examination duties were finished, he served concurrently as acting vice director in the Ministry of War. He was formally appointed vice minister of war, then left office to observe mourning for his father. After mourning he was recalled as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and was granted the gold-and-purple robes of high office. In the eighth month of the third year, while retaining his existing rank, he became co-manager of affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
5
時裴度薦李德裕，將大用。 德裕自浙西入朝，為中人助宗閔者所沮，復出鎮。 尋引牛僧孺同知政事，二人唱和，凡德裕之黨皆逐之。 累轉中書侍郎、集賢大學士。 七年，德裕作相。 六月，罷宗閔知政事，檢校禮部尚書、同平章事、興元尹、山南西道節度使。
At that time Pei Du recommended Li Deyu and intended to give him a major appointment. Deyu entered court from Zhexi, but was blocked by eunuchs who supported Zongmin and was sent out again to govern a circuit. Soon afterward Zongmin brought in Niu Sengru to share in governing affairs. Working in concert, the two drove away everyone in Deyu's faction. He rose in succession to vice director of the Secretariat and grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. In the seventh year, Deyu became chief minister. In the sixth month, Zongmin was removed from governing affairs and was appointed concurrently as minister of rites, co-manager of affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery, prefect of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Shanan West Circuit.
6
宗閔為吏部侍郎時，因駙馬都尉沈結托女學士宋若憲及知樞密楊承和，二人數稱之於上前，故獲徵用。 及德裕秉政，群邪不悅，而鄭註、李訓深惡之。 文宗乃復召宗閔於興元，為中書侍郎、平章事，命德裕代宗閔為興元尹。 既再得權位，輔之以訓、註，尤恣所欲，進封襄武侯，食邑千戶。
When Zongmin was vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, he gained appointment through the imperial son-in-law Shen Jietuo, the female academician Song Ruoxian, and the privy-council director Yang Chenghe, who repeatedly praised him before the emperor. When Deyu took power, the corrupt were displeased, while Zheng Zhu and Li Xun deeply hated him. Emperor Wenzong then recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan, appointing him vice director of the Secretariat and manager of affairs, and ordered Deyu to replace Zongmin as prefect of Xingyuan. Once he had regained power, aided by Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, he indulged his desires all the more. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangwu with a fief of one thousand households.
7
九年六月，京兆尹楊虞卿得罪，宗閔極言救解，文宗怒叱之曰：「爾嘗謂鄭覃是妖氣，今作妖，覃耶、爾耶？ 」翌日，貶明州刺史，尋再貶處州長史。 七月，鄭註發沈、宋若憲事，內官楊承和、韋元素、沈及若憲姻黨坐貶者十餘人，又貶宗閔潮州司戶。 時訓、註竊弄威權，凡不附己者，目為宗閔、德裕之黨，貶逐無虛日，中外震駭，連月陰晦，人情不安。 九月詔曰：
In the sixth month of the ninth year, when Metropolitan Prefect Yang Yuqing fell afoul of the court, Zongmin spoke at length in his defense. Emperor Wenzong angrily rebuked him, saying, "You once said that Zheng Tan was an evil influence. Now who is working evil—Tan, or you?" The next day Zongmin was demoted to prefect of Ming, and soon afterward was demoted again to chief administrator of Chuzhou. In the seventh month, Zheng Zhu exposed the affair involving Shen and Song Ruoxian. More than ten inner-court officials, including Yang Chenghe, Wei Yuansu, Shen, and Ruoxian's relatives by marriage, were demoted on account of it, and Zongmin was demoted again to registrar of Chaozhou. At the time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu usurped authority. Anyone who did not side with them was labeled a partisan of Zongmin or Deyu, and demotions and banishments came day after day without pause. Court and country alike were shaken with alarm; for months the skies stayed overcast, and public sentiment grew uneasy. In the ninth month an edict declared:
8
朕承天纘歷，燭理不明，勞虛襟以求賢，勵寬德以容眾。 頃者，或臺輔乖弼違之道，而具僚扇朋附之風； 翕然相從，實篸彜憲。 致使薰蕕共器，賢不肖並馳； 退跡者成後時之夫，登門者有迎吠之客。 繆戾之氣，堙郁和平，而望陰陽順時，疵癘不作； 朝廷清肅，班列和安，自古及今，未嘗有也。 今既再申朝典，一變澆風，掃清朋比之徒，匡飭貞廉之俗。 凡百卿士，惟新令猷。 如聞周行之中，尚蓄疑懼，或有妄相指目，令不自安，今斯曠然，明喻朕意。 應與宗閔、德裕或親或故及門生舊吏等，除今日已前黜遠之外，一切不問。 各安職業，勿復為嫌。
We have received Heaven's mandate and succeeded to the throne, yet Our understanding of governance has not been clear enough. We have opened Our heart to seek the worthy and cultivated broad virtue to embrace the multitude. Recently, some chief ministers have departed from the way of assisting and correcting the throne, while assembled officials have fanned the wind of partisan attachment; they have flocked together in mutual adherence, truly piercing the great norms and statutes of governance. This has caused the worthy and the unworthy to share the same vessel and to advance side by side; those who withdrew became men left behind by the times, while those who came to the gate found only fawning partisans. Wayward and perverse influences have choked off harmony, yet We still expect yin and yang to follow their seasons and pestilence not to arise; the court to be pure and solemn, and the ranks to be harmonious and secure—from antiquity to the present, there has never been such a thing. Now We have again proclaimed the court's canonical standards, wholly changed the corrupt wind, swept away partisan cliques, and restored the custom of integrity and probity. Let all you ministers and officials renew your good counsel. We have heard that among the court ranks suspicion and fear still linger, and that some recklessly point fingers at one another, leaving others ill at ease. Now We make this clear and openly explain Our intent. All who are related to Zongmin or Deyu by kinship or old acquaintance, as well as their students and former subordinates, apart from those already banished before today, shall altogether go unquestioned. Each shall rest secure in his office and no longer harbor grievances against one another.
9
文宗以二李朋黨，繩之不能去，嘗謂侍臣曰：「去河北賊非難，去此朋黨實難。 」宗閔雖驟放黜，竟免李訓之禍。
Because of the partisan cliques of the two Lis, Emperor Wenzong could not remove them even when he tried to restrain them. He once told his attending ministers, "Removing the rebels of Hebei is not hard; removing these partisan cliques is truly hard." Although Zongmin was suddenly dismissed and banished, he ultimately escaped the disaster brought by Li Xun.
10
，量移衢州司馬。 三年，楊嗣復輔政，與宗閔厚善，欲拔用之，而畏鄭覃沮議，乃托中人密諷於上。 上以嗣復故，因紫宸對，謂宰相曰：「宗閔在外四五年，宜別授一官。 」鄭覃曰：「陛下憐其地遠，宜移近內地三五百里，不可再用奸邪。 陛下若欲用宗閔，臣請先退。 」陳夷行曰：「比者，宗閔得罪，以朋黨之故，恕死為幸。 寶歷初，李續之、張又新、蘇景胤等，朋比奸險，幾傾朝廷，時號『八關十六子』。 」李玨曰：「主此事者，罪在逢吉。 李續之居喪服闋，不可不與一官，臣恐中外衣冠，交興議論，非為續之輩也。 」夷行曰：「昔舜逐四兇天下治。 朝廷求理，何惜此十數纖人？ 」嗣復曰：「事貴得中，不可但徇憎愛。 」上曰：「與一郡可也。 」鄭覃曰：「與郡太優，止可洪州司馬耳。 」夷行曰：「宗閔養成鄭註之惡，幾覆邦家，國之巨蠹也。 」嗣復曰：「比者，陛下欲加鄭註官，宗閔不肯，陛下亦當記憶。 」覃曰：「嗣復黨庇宗閔。 臣觀宗閔之惡，甚於李林甫。 」嗣復曰：「覃語大過。 昔玄宗季年，委用林甫，妒賢害能，破人家族。 宗閔在位，固無此事。 況太和末，宗閔、德裕同時得罪。 二年之間，德裕再領重鎮，而宗閔未離貶所。 陛下懲惡勸善，進退之理宜均，非臣獨敢黨庇。 昨殷侑與韓益奏官及章服，臣以益前年犯贓，未可其奏； 鄭覃托臣雲『幸且勿論。 』孰為黨庇？ 」翌日，以宗閔為杭州刺史。 四年冬，遷太子賓客，分司東都。 時鄭覃、陳夷行罷相，嗣復方再拔用宗閔知政事，俄而文宗崩。
He was transferred by graded demotion to assistant administrator of Quzhou. In the third year, Yang Sifu assisted in governance. He was on close terms with Zongmin and wished to promote him, but feared that Zheng Tan would block the proposal, so he had a eunuch secretly hint at it to the emperor. Because of Sifu, during an audience in the Zichen Hall the emperor said to the chief ministers, "Zongmin has been outside the court for four or five years. He should be given another office." Zheng Tan said, "If Your Majesty pities him for being so far away, he should be moved to within three or five hundred li of the inner regions. One must not employ the wicked again." If Your Majesty wishes to employ Zongmin, I ask first to withdraw from office. Chen Yixing said, "Recently Zongmin offended because of partisan cliques. It was good fortune enough that he was spared death." At the beginning of the Baoli reign, Li Xuzhi, Zhang Youxin, Su Jingyin, and others formed a corrupt and treacherous clique that nearly overturned the court. At the time they were called the "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons." Li Jue said, "The one chiefly responsible for this affair was Fengji." Li Xuzhi has completed mourning and cannot be denied some office. I fear that officials inside and outside the court will all begin to talk about it—not for the sake of Xuzhi and his like alone. Yixing said, "In antiquity, when Shun drove out the Four Evils, the realm was well governed." If the court seeks good order, why spare these dozen or so petty men? Sifu said, "Affairs must strike the mean; one cannot simply follow personal hatred or favor alone." The emperor said, "Giving him a prefecture would be acceptable." Zheng Tan said, "A prefecture is too generous. He should receive only the post of assistant administrator of Hongzhou." Yixing said, "Zongmin nurtured the evil of Zheng Zhu and nearly overturned the state. He is a great bane to the realm." Sifu said, "Recently, when Your Majesty wished to promote Zheng Zhu, Zongmin refused to agree. Your Majesty should remember that as well." Tan said, "Sifu is shielding Zongmin as a partisan." In my view, Zongmin's wickedness surpasses that of Li Linfu. Sifu said, "Tan's words go too far." In the late years of Emperor Xuanzong, he entrusted power to Linfu, who envied the worthy, harmed the capable, and destroyed families. When Zongmin held office, there was certainly nothing of that sort. Moreover, at the end of the Taihe reign, Zongmin and Deyu both offended at the same time. Within two years, Deyu twice took command of major circuits, while Zongmin had not yet left his place of banishment. Your Majesty punishes evil and encourages good. The principle of advancement and withdrawal should be even-handed. It is not that I alone dare to shield a partisan. Yesterday Yin You and Han Yi memorialized about office and ceremonial robes. I held that Yi had committed embezzlement the year before last and could not approve their memorial; Zheng Tan asked me, saying, "For now, please do not press the matter." Who then is shielding a partisan? The next day, Zongmin was appointed prefect of Hangzhou. In the winter of the fourth year, he was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent and served at the Eastern Capital in a nominal post. At that time Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing had been removed as chief ministers, and Sifu was just about to promote Zongmin again to share in governing affairs when Emperor Wenzong suddenly died.
11
會昌初，李德裕秉政，嗣復、李玨皆竄嶺表。 三年，劉稹據澤潞叛。 德裕以宗閔素與劉從諫厚，上黨近東都，宗閔分司非便，出為封州刺史。 又發其舊事，貶郴州司馬，卒於貶所。
At the beginning of the Huichang reign, when Li Deyu took power, Sifu and Li Jue were both banished to the regions south of the Ling Range. In the third year, Liu Zhen seized Ze and Lu and rebelled. Deyu, because Zongmin had long been on close terms with Liu Congjian and because Shangdang was near the Eastern Capital, held that it was unsuitable for Zongmin to serve there in a nominal post, and sent him out as prefect of Feng. Deyu also exposed his old offenses, and Zongmin was demoted to assistant administrator of Chen. He died in his place of banishment.
12
子琨、瓚，大中朝皆進士擢第。 令狐綯作相，特加獎拔。 瓚自員外郎知制誥，歷中書舍人、翰林學士。 綯罷相，出為桂管觀察使。 御軍無政，為卒所逐，貶死。
His sons Kun and Zan both passed the jinshi examination during the Dazhong reign. When Linghu Tao became chief minister, he gave them special encouragement and promotion. Zan, starting as a vice director, was put in charge of drafting edicts and served in succession as vice director in the Secretariat and Hanlin academician. When Tao was removed as chief minister, Zan was sent out as observation commissioner of Gui. He governed the army without proper discipline, was driven out by his soldiers, and died in exile after demotion.
13
自天寶艱難之後，宗室子弟，賢而立功者，唯鄭王、曹王子孫耳。 夷簡再從季父汧國公勉，德宗朝宰相。 夷簡諸弟夷亮、夷則、夷範，皆登進士第。 宗閔弟宗冉。 宗冉子深、湯。 湯累官至給事中，咸通中踐更臺閣，知名於時。 楊嗣復楊嗣復，字繼之，僕射於陵子也。 初，於陵十九登進十第，二十再登博學宏詞科，謂補潤州句容尉。 浙西觀察使韓滉有知人之鑒，見之甚悅。 滉有愛女，方擇佳婿，謂其妻柳氏曰：「吾閱人多矣，無如楊生貴而有壽，生子必為宰相。 」於陵秩滿，寓居揚州而生嗣復。 後滉見之，撫其首曰：「名位果逾於父，楊門之慶也。 」因字曰慶門。
After the hardships of the Tianbao era, among the sons and younger kinsmen of the imperial clan who were worthy and established merit, there were only the descendants of the Princes of Zheng and Cao. Yijian's second cousin once removed was Prince Qian, Gong Mian, who had served as chief minister under Emperor Dezong. Yi Jian's younger brothers Yi Liang, Yi Ze, and Yi Fan all attained jinshi rank. Li Zongmin's younger brother was Zong Ran. Zong Ran's sons were Shen and Tang. Tang eventually reached the post of Supervising Secretary; under the Xiantong emperor he rotated through offices in the capital secretariat and won wide renown. Yang Sifu (zi Jizhi) was the son of Grand Counselor Yang Yuling. In his youth Yang Yuling passed the jinshi at nineteen and the boxue hongci examination at twenty, then received appointment as assistant magistrate of Jurong in Runzhou. Han Huang, Commissioner of the Zhexi Circuit, was famed for discerning men's true worth, and was deeply impressed when he met Yang Yuling. Han Huang had a cherished daughter and was seeking a worthy match; he told his wife Lady Liu, "I have seen countless men, yet none like young Yang—of noble mien and destined for long life; sons born to him will surely reach the chancellorship." After Yuling's term expired he settled in Yangzhou, and there Yang Sifu was born. Later Han Huang met the boy, stroked his head, and said, "Your name and station will indeed exceed your father's—a blessing upon the house of Yang." He therefore bestowed upon him the courtesy name Qingmen, "Celebration Gate."
14
嗣復七八歲時已能秉筆為文。 年二十，進士擢第。 二十一，又登博學宏詞科，釋褐秘書省校書郎。 遷右拾遺，直史館。 以嗣復深於禮學，改太常博士。 ，累遷至刑部員外郎。 鄭餘慶為詳定禮儀使，奏為判官，改禮部員外郎。 時父於陵為戶部侍郎，嗣復上言與父同省非便，請換他官。 詔曰：「應同司官有大功以下親者，但非連判及勾檢之官並官長，則不在回避之限。 如官署同，職司異，雖父子兄弟無所避嫌。 」再遷兵部郎中。 十月，以庫部郎中知制誥，正拜中書舍人。
By the age of seven or eight Sifu could already wield the brush and write compositions. At twenty he passed the jinshi examination. At twenty-one he passed the boxue hongci examination and, upon donning official robes, was appointed collator in the Secretariat. He was promoted to Right Reminder and assigned to duty in the History Office. On account of Sifu's deep mastery of ritual studies, he was transferred to the post of Erudite in the Grand Ritual Office. He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. When Zheng Yuqing served as Commissioner for Determining Ritual Protocols, he recommended Sifu as his aide and had him transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites. At the time his father Yuling was Vice Minister of Revenue; Sifu memorialized the throne that serving alongside his father in the same ministry was unseemly and requested transfer elsewhere. The emperor replied by edict: "When officials of one department share kinship within the degree of great merit or closer, they need not withdraw unless they serve as consecutive judges, audit officers, or department heads—those cases fall outside the rule of avoidance." When the department is shared but the duties differ, even fathers and sons or brothers need not shun one another. He was promoted again to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War. In the tenth month, while serving as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Stores he was charged with drafting edicts, and was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
15
嗣復與牛僧孺、李宗閔皆權德輿貢舉門生，情義相得，進退取舍，多與之同。 四年，僧孺作相，欲薦拔大用，又以於陵為東都留守。 未歷相位，乃令嗣復權知禮部侍郎。 二月，選貢士六十八人，後多至達官。 文宗即位，拜戶部侍郎。 以父於陵太子少傅致仕，年高多疾，懇辭侍養，不之許。 ，丁父憂免。 七年三月，起為尚書左丞。 其年宗閔罷相，德裕輔政。 七月，以嗣復檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度觀察等使。 九年，宗閔復知政事。 三月，以嗣復檢校戶部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事、觀察處置等使。
Sifu, Niu Sengru, and Li Zongmin had all been examination disciples of Quan Deyu; united in friendship, they largely moved together in office—advancing, withdrawing, and choosing sides as one. In the fourth year Niu Sengru took the chancellorship and sought to elevate Sifu to high office; meanwhile Yuling served as Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital. Before Sengru himself had held the chancellorship, he had Sifu serve as acting Vice Minister of Rites. In the second month he selected sixty-eight tribute scholars, many of whom later rose to eminent posts. When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Sifu was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue. When his father Yuling retired as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, aged and often ill, Sifu pleaded earnestly to withdraw and tend him at home, but the throne would not allow it. He then mourned his father's death and left office. In the third month of the seventh year he was recalled as Left Vice Director of the Ministries. That year Li Zongmin left the chancellorship and Li Deyu took up the reins of government. In the seventh month Sifu was appointed provisional Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zizhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of the Jiannan East Circuit. In the ninth year Li Zongmin returned to direct the affairs of state. In the third month Sifu was appointed provisional Minister of Revenue, Governor of Chengdu, and Deputy Military Governor of the Jiannan West Circuit with full authority over the command and its observation affairs.
16
十月，入為戶部侍郎，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。 三年正月，與同列李玨並以本官同平章事，領使如故，進階金紫，弘農伯，食邑七百戶。 上以幣輕錢重，問鹽鐵使何以去其太甚？ 嗣復曰：「此事累朝制置未得，但且禁銅，未可變法。 法變擾人，終亦未罷去弊。 」李玨曰：「禁銅之令，朝廷常典，但行之不嚴，不如無令。 今江淮已南，銅器成肆，市井逐利者，銷錢一緡，可為數器，售利三四倍。 遠民不知法令，率以為常。 縱國家加爐鑄錢，何以供銷鑄之弊？ 所以禁銅之令，不得不嚴。 」
In the tenth month he returned to court as Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport for all circuits. In the first month of the third year he and his colleague Li Jue were both made Co-Chancellors while keeping their existing offices and commissions; Sifu was raised to golden-purple rank, enfeoffed as Marquis of Hongnong with seven hundred taxable households. Observing that coin was debased while cash grew scarce, the emperor asked the Salt and Iron Commissioner how the worst of the imbalance might be remedied. Sifu replied, "Successive courts have failed to settle this; for now we should enforce the ban on copper and not rashly alter the law." Alter the law and you trouble the people, yet the evil is not finally removed. Li Jue said, "The prohibition on copper is long-established court law—but a law loosely enforced might as well not exist." Today south of the Yangtze and Huai, copperware shops line the markets; townsmen chasing profit melt coin by the string into several vessels and sell them for three- or fourfold gain. Peasants in remote districts, ignorant of the law, take this for ordinary practice. Even if the state poured more furnaces into minting, how could it keep pace with the coin lost to illicit melting? That is why the ban on copper must be enforced without laxity. "
17
八月，紫宸奏事，曰：「聖人在上，野無遺賢。 陸洿上疏論兵，雖不中時事，意亦可獎。 閑居蘇州累年，宜與一官。 」李玨曰：「士子趨競者多，若獎陸洿，貪夫知勸矣。 昨竇洵直論事，陛下賞之以幣帛，況與陸洿官耶？ 」帝曰：「洵直獎其直心，不言事之當否。 」鄭覃曰：「若苞藏則不可知。 」嗣復曰：「臣深知洵直無邪惡，所奏陸洿官，尚未奉聖旨。 」鄭覃曰：「陛下須防朋黨。 」嗣復曰：「鄭覃疑臣朋黨，乞陛下放臣歸去。 」因拜乞罷免。 李玨曰：「比來朋黨，近亦稍弭。 」覃曰：「近有小朋黨生。 」帝曰：「此輩雕喪向盡。 」覃曰：「楊漢公、張又新、李續之即今尚在。 」玨曰：「今有邊事論奏。 」覃曰：「論邊事安危，臣不如玨； 嫉惡則玨不如臣。 」嗣復曰：「臣聞左右佩劍，彼此相笑。 臣今不知鄭覃指誰為朋黨。 」因當香案前奏曰：「臣待罪宰相，不能申夔、龍之道，唯以朋黨見譏，必乞陛下罷臣鼎職。 」上慰勉之。 文宗方以政事委嗣復，惡覃言切。
In the eighth month, speaking in the Purple Hall, he said, "Under a sage ruler no talent languishes in obscurity." Lu Yu had memorialized on military matters; though untimely, his purpose deserved commendation. Having lived in seclusion at Suzhou for many years, he should be granted a post. Li Jue said, "Too many scholars scramble for favor; reward Lu Yu and the covetous will take it as invitation." Only yesterday Dou Xunzhi spoke forth on policy and Your Majesty rewarded him with silks—would you now grant Lu Yu an office as well? The emperor said, "I rewarded Xunzhi for the honesty of his heart, not for the correctness of his counsel." Zheng Tan said, "When men conceal their true intent, who can discern it?" Sifu said, "I know Xunzhi to be free of evil design; as for my recommendation of an office for Lu Yu, I have not yet received Your Majesty's command." Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty must beware of cliques." Sifu said, "Zheng Tan accuses me of clique-making; I beg Your Majesty to dismiss me and let me go home." He bowed low and pleaded to be relieved of office. Li Jue said, "The factional quarrels of recent times have already begun to quiet." Zheng Tan said, "Of late small cliques have sprung up again." The emperor said, "That faction is nearly spent—its carved tombs almost full." Zheng Tan said, "Yang Hangong, Zhang Youxin, and Li Xuzhi yet live." Li Jue said, "Today the court has frontier business to discuss." Zheng Tan said, "When it comes to weighing the peril of the frontier, I am no match for Jue;" but in detesting wickedness, Jue is no match for me." Sifu said, "I have heard that swordsmen at one another's sides are the first to mock each other's blades." Today I do not know whom Zheng Tan has in mind when he speaks of cliques. He then addressed the throne before the incense table: "I stand guilty as chancellor, unable to uphold the sage governance of Kui and Long; reproached solely as a faction-maker, I beg Your Majesty to strip me of this post." The emperor soothed and urged him to remain. Emperor Wenzong had already entrusted the governance to Sifu and took offense at Zheng Tan's cutting speech.
18
帝延英謂宰臣曰：「人傳符讖之語，自何而來？ 」嗣復對曰：「漢光武好以讖書決事，近代隋文帝亦信此言，自是，此說日滋，只如班彪《王命論》所引，蓋矯意以止賊亂，非所重也。 」李玨曰：「喪亂之時，佐命者務神符命； 理平之代，只合推諸人事。 」上曰：「卿言是也。 」帝又曰：「天後用人，有自布衣至宰相者，當時還得力否？ 」嗣復曰：「天後重行刑辟，輕用官爵，皆自圖之計耳。 凡用人之道，歷試方見其能否。 當艱難之時，或須拔擢，無事之日，不如且循資級。 古人拔卒為將，非治平之時，蓋不獲已而用之也。 」上又問新修《開元政要》，敘致何如。 嗣復曰：「臣等未見。 陛下若欲遺之子孫，則請宣付臣等，參詳可否。 玄宗或好遊畋，或好聲色，與貞觀之政不同，故取舍須當，方堪流傳。 」
At Yanying Hall the emperor asked his chancellors, "Prophetic sayings circulate among the people—where do they arise?" Sifu answered, "Han Guangwu loved to decide policy by apocryphal prophecy; Sui Wendi trusted such talk as well, and from that day the doctrine spread. Even what Ban Biao's Discourse on the Mandate of Kings cites was largely artifice to quell rebellion—not wisdom to be revered." Li Jue said, "In ages of ruin and upheaval, men who rise to serve the mandate lean upon omens and fate;" in an age of peace one should look only to human effort." The emperor said, "You speak rightly." The emperor also asked, "When Empress Wu raised men from commoners to the chancellorship, did they prove capable?" Sifu said, "Empress Wu relied heavily on punishment and lightly on rank—all calculated for her own ends." The proper way to employ men is to test them through service before judging their capacity. In crisis one may need to lift men abruptly; in calm times it is better to advance them by seniority. The ancients made generals of common soldiers—not in tranquil ages, but only when necessity left no other course." The emperor next asked about the newly edited Essentials of Governance from the Kaiyuan Era—what of its arrangement and tone? Sifu said, "We have not yet seen the text." If Your Majesty means to bequeath it to posterity, let it be sent to us that we may judge what should remain and what should not. Emperor Xuanzong indulged at times in the hunt and at times in pleasure—far from the governance of the Zhenguan era; what is preserved and what is cut must be chosen with care if the work is to endure." "
19
四年五月，上問延英政事，逐日何人記錄監修？ 李玨曰：「是臣職司。 」陳夷行曰：「宰相所錄，必當自伐，聖德即將掩之。 臣所以頻言，不欲威權在下。 」玨曰：「夷行此言，是疑宰相中有賣威權、貨刑賞者。 不然，何自為宰相而出此言？ 臣累奏求退，若得王傅，臣之幸也。 」鄭覃曰：「陛下、二年政事至好，三年、四年漸不如前。 」嗣復曰：「元年、二年是鄭覃、夷行用事，三年、四年臣與李玨同之。 臣蒙聖慈擢處相位，不能悉心奉職。 鄭覃云『三年之後，一年不如一年』，臣之罪也。 陛下縱不誅夷，臣合自求泯滅。 」因叩頭曰：「臣今日便辭玉階，不敢更入中書。 」即趨去。 上令中使召還，勞之曰：「鄭覃失言，卿何及此？ 」覃起謝曰：「臣性愚拙，言無顧慮。 近日事亦漸好，未免些些不公，亦無甚處。 臣亦不獨斥嗣復，遽何至此。 所為若是，乃嗣復不容臣耳。 」嗣復曰：「陛下不以臣微才，用為中書侍郎。 時政善否，其責在臣。 陛下月費俸錢數十萬，時新珍異，必先賜與，蓋欲輔佐聖明，臻於至理。 既一年不如一年，非惟臣合得罪，亦上累聖德。 伏請別命賢能，許臣休退。 」上曰：「鄭覃之言偶然耳，奚執咎耶？ 」嗣復數日不入，上表請罷。 帝方委用，乃罷鄭覃、夷行知政事。 自是，政歸嗣復，進加門下侍郎。 明年正月，文宗崩。
In the fifth month of the fourth year, questioning policy at Yanying Hall, the emperor asked who kept and oversaw the daily record of court business. Li Jue said, "That falls to me." Chen Yixing said, "When chancellors keep the record they inevitably glorify themselves—and the emperor's true merit will be eclipsed." I have raised this again and again because I will not see authority lodged below the throne. Li Jue said, "Yixing's remark suggests he suspects some chancellor of peddling power and bartering punishments and rewards." Otherwise why, being a chancellor himself, would he say such a thing? I have repeatedly asked to withdraw; if I might become Royal Tutor, I would count myself fortunate. Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty, the first two years of your reign went well; the third and fourth have steadily declined." Sifu said, "The first two years belonged to Zheng Tan and Chen Yixing; the third and fourth my colleague Li Jue and I shared." Raised to the chancellorship by your grace, I have failed to serve with my whole heart. When Zheng Tan says that after the third year each year has grown worse, the fault is mine. Even if Your Majesty does not punish Yixing, I ought to remove myself from sight. He kowtowed and said, "Today I quit the jade steps and will not again set foot in the Secretariat." He turned and hastened out. The emperor sent a palace envoy to recall him and said gently, "Zheng Tan misspoke—why take it so hard?" Zheng Tan rose and apologized: "I am dull by nature and spoke without due care." Affairs have lately improved somewhat; minor injustices remain, but nothing of great moment. I did not censure Sifu alone—why has it come to this so suddenly? If he behaves thus, it is because Sifu will not tolerate me. Li Sifu said, "Your Majesty, overlooking my modest gifts, appointed me Vice Director of the Secretariat." Whether the times are well or ill governed, the burden is mine. Your Majesty pays me hundreds of thousands each month in salary, and seasonal delicacies and rare gifts are always sent to me first—all so that I may aid Your Majesty in bringing the realm to perfect order. Each year has been worse than the last—not only should I be punished, but Your Majesty's own virtue is diminished thereby. I humbly ask that another worthy be appointed in my place and that I be allowed to withdraw from office. The emperor said, "Zheng Tan spoke casually—why take offense?" Li Sifu stayed away from court for several days and submitted a memorial asking to be removed from office. The emperor was then relying on Li Sifu, and dismissed Zheng Tan and Li Yexing from directing the government. From then on power returned to Li Sifu, who was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery. In the first month of the following year, Emperor Wenzong died.
20
先是，以敬宗子陳王為皇太子。 中尉仇士良違遺令立武宗。 武宗之立，既非宰相本意，甚薄執政之臣。 其年秋，李德裕自淮南入輔政。 九月，出嗣復為湖南觀察使。 明年，誅樞密薛季稜、劉弘逸。 中人言：「二人頃附嗣復、李玨，不利於陛下。 」武宗性急，立命中使往湖南、桂管，殺嗣復與玨。 宰相崔鄲、崔珙等亟請開延英，因極言國朝故事，大臣非惡逆顯著，未有誅戮者，願陛下復思其宜。 帝良久改容曰：「朕纘嗣之際，宰相何嘗比數。 李玨、季稜志在扶冊陳王，嗣復、弘逸志在樹立安王。 立陳王猶是文宗遺旨，嗣復欲立安王，全是希楊妃意旨。 嗣復嘗與妃書云：『姑姑何不敩則天臨朝？ 』」珙等曰：「此事曖昧，真虛難辨。 」帝曰：「楊妃曾臥疾，妃弟玄思，文宗令入內侍疾月餘，此時通導意旨。 朕細問內人，情狀皎然，我不欲宣出於外。 向使安王得志，我豈有今日？ 然為卿等恕之。 」乃追潭、桂二中使，再貶嗣復潮州刺史。
Earlier, Emperor Jingzong's son, the Prince of Chen, had been named crown prince. The commandant of the Right Army, Qiu Shiliang, defied the dying emperor's command and enthroned Emperor Wuzong. Because Wuzong's enthronement had not been the chief ministers' wish, he held little regard for the men then in power. That autumn Li Deyu came from Huainan to join the government. In the ninth month Li Sifu was sent out as military governor of Hunan. The following year the palace secretaries Xue Jiling and Liu Hongyi were put to death. Palace eunuchs said, "These two lately sided with Li Sifu and Li Jue, to Your Majesty's harm." Wuzong was hot-tempered by nature and at once ordered palace envoys to Hunan and Guiguan to kill Li Sifu and Li Jue. The chief ministers Cui Tan and Cui Gong urgently requested an audience in Yanying Hall and spoke at length of dynastic precedent: no minister who was not openly guilty of treason had ever been executed. They asked the emperor to reconsider. After a long pause the emperor's face changed and he said, "When I succeeded to the throne, were the chief ministers ever on my side?" Li Jue and Xue Jiling meant to install the Prince of Chen; Li Sifu and Liu Hongyi meant to establish the Prince of An. Installing the Prince of Chen was still in accord with Wenzong's dying command; Li Sifu wished to install the Prince of An solely to please Consort Yang. Li Sifu once wrote to the consort: 'Aunt, why not take Empress Wu as your model and hold court?' Cui Gong and the others said, "This matter is unclear; truth and falsehood are hard to tell apart." The emperor said, "Consort Yang once fell ill. Wenzong had her younger brother Xuan Si enter the palace to attend her for more than a month, and at that time he carried their messages back and forth." I questioned the palace women closely; the facts are perfectly clear. I do not wish to make this public. If the Prince of An had had his way, would I be emperor today? Yet for your sake I will spare them. He then recalled the envoys bound for Tan and Gui, and Li Sifu was demoted again to prefect of Chaozhou.
21
宣宗即位，徵拜吏部尚書。 ，自潮陽還，至岳州病，一日而卒，時年六十六。 贈左僕射，謚曰孝穆。
When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, Li Sifu was summoned and appointed minister of personnel. On his way back from Chaoyang he fell ill at Yuezhou and died within a day, at the age of sixty-six. He was posthumously made Left Vice Director and given the posthumous name Xiaomu.
22
子損、授、技、拭、捴，而授最賢。
His sons were Sun, Shou, Ji, Shi, and Zong; of them Shou was the most worthy.
23
授，字得符，進士擢第，釋褐從事諸侯府，入為鄠縣尉、集賢校理。 歷監察御史、殿中，分務東臺。 再遷司勛員外郎、洛陽令、兵部員外郎。 李福為東都留守，奏充判官，改兵部郎中，由吏部拜左諫議大夫、給事中，出為河南尹。 盧攜作相，召拜工部侍郎。 黃巢犯京師，僖宗幸蜀，徵拜戶部侍郎。 以母病，求散秩，改秘書監分司。 車駕還，拜兵部侍郎。 宰相有報怨者，改左散騎常侍、國子祭酒，又轉太子賓客。 從昭宗在華下，改刑部尚書、太子少保。 卒，贈左僕射。
Shou, whose courtesy name was Defu, passed the jinshi examination. After taking his first office he served on the staffs of regional lords, then entered the capital as magistrate of Hu County and collator in the Office of Gathered Worthies. He served as imperial censor and palace censor, with duties on the Eastern Censorate. He was promoted in turn to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel, magistrate of Luoyang, and assistant director in the Ministry of War. When Li Fu served as regent of the Eastern Capital, Shou was recommended as his administrative aide. He was then made director in the Ministry of War, and through the Ministry of Personnel was appointed left remonstrance counselor and attendant censor before being sent out as intendant of Henan. When Lu Xie became chief minister, Shou was summoned and appointed vice minister of works. When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Shou was summoned and appointed vice minister of revenue. Because his mother was ill, he asked for a nominal post and was made concurrent director of the Secretariat. When the court returned to the capital, he was appointed vice minister of war. A chief minister who bore a grudge against him had him transferred to left regular attendant and grand master of the Imperial Academy, and later to mentor to the heir apparent. When he followed Emperor Zhaozong to Huaxia, he was made minister of justice and junior mentor to the heir apparent. He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director.
24
子煚，字公隱，進士及第，再遷左拾遺。 昭宗初即位，喜遊宴，不恤時事，煚上疏極諫，帝面賜緋袍象笏。 崔安潛出鎮青州，辟為支使。 不至鎮，改太常博士。 歷主客、戶部二員外郎。 關中亂，崔胤引硃全忠入京師，乃挈家避地湖南，官終諫議大夫。
His son Jiong, whose courtesy name was Gongyin, passed the jinshi examination and was twice promoted to left supplementer. When Zhaozong first came to the throne he delighted in feasting and neglected affairs of state. Jiong submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance, and the emperor personally bestowed on him a crimson robe and ivory tablet. When Cui Anqian went out to command Qingzhou, he recruited Jiong as his staff envoy. Before he reached his post, Jiong was transferred to doctor of the Court of Ceremonies. He served as assistant director in the ministries of rites for receptions and of revenue. When the Guanzhong region fell into chaos and Cui Yin brought Zhu Quanzhong into the capital, Jiong moved his family to Hunan for safety. His highest office was remonstrance counselor.
25
損，字子默，以廕受官，為藍田尉。 三遷京兆府司錄參軍，入為殿中侍御史。 家在新昌里，與宰相路巖第相接。 巖以地狹，欲易損馬廄廣之，遣人致意。 時損伯叔昆仲在朝者十餘人，相與議曰：「家門損益恃時相，何可拒之？ 」損曰：「非也。 凡尺寸地，非吾等所有。 先人舊業，安可以奉權臣？ 窮達，命也。 」巖不悅。 會差制使鞫獄黔中，乃遣損使焉。 逾年而還，改戶部員外郎、洛陽縣令。 入為吏部員外，出為絳州刺史。 路巖罷相，徵拜給事中，遷京兆尹。 盧攜作相，有宿憾，復拜給事中，出為陜虢觀察使。 時軍亂，逐前使崔蕘。 損至，盡誅其亂首。 逾年，改青州刺史、御史大夫、淄青節度使。 又檢校刑部尚書、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度使。 未赴鄆，復留青州，卒於鎮。
Sun, whose courtesy name was Zimo, received office by yin privilege and served as magistrate of Lantian. After three promotions he became recorder in the Jingzhao prefecture government, then entered office as palace attendant censor. His family home in Xinchang Ward stood next to the mansion of Chief Minister Lu Yan. Lu Yan, finding his grounds too cramped, wished to swap Sun's stable for more space and sent a messenger to propose the exchange. At the time more than ten of Sun's uncles and brothers held office at court. They discussed the matter together and said, "The family's fortunes depend on the current chief minister—how can we refuse?" Sun said, "No." Not one inch of ground is truly ours to dispose of. These are our forefathers' holdings—how could we hand them over to a powerful minister? Rise and fall are a matter of fate. Lu Yan was displeased. When an imperial commissioner was sent to investigate cases in Qianzhong, Sun was dispatched on that mission. After more than a year he returned and was made assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue and magistrate of Luoyang county. He entered office as assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou. When Lu Yan was removed from the chancellorship, Sun was summoned as attendant censor and promoted to intendant of Jingzhao. When Lu Xie became chief minister, still bearing an old grievance, Sun was again made attendant censor and sent out as military governor of Shan-Guo. At the time the army mutinied and drove out the former commissioner Cui Rao. When Sun arrived, he executed all the ringleaders of the mutiny. After more than a year he was made prefect of Qingzhou, censor-in-chief, and military governor of Zi-Qing. He was also made acting minister of justice, prefect of Yanzhou, and military governor of the Tianping Army. Before he could proceed to Yanzhou, he was kept at Qingzhou and died there in office.
26
技進士及第，位至中書舍人。
Ji passed the jinshi examination and rose to drafter in the Secretariat.
27
拭官終考功員外郎。 捴終兵部郎中。 拭、捴並進士擢第。 楊虞卿楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。 祖燕客。 父寧，貞元中為長安尉。 少有棲遁之志，以處士徵入朝。 有口辯，優遊公卿間。 竇參尤重之，會參貶，仕進不達而卒。
Shi's last office was assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel for merits. Zong's last office was director in the Ministry of War. Shi and Zong both passed the jinshi examination. Yang Yuqing—Yang Yuqing, whose courtesy name was Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture. His grandfather was Yanke. His father Ning served as magistrate of Chang'an during the Zhenyuan reign. From youth he wished to live in seclusion; summoned as a hermit scholar, he entered court. He was eloquent and moved at ease among high ministers and nobles. Dou Can especially valued him, but when Can was demoted he never advanced in office and died.
28
虞卿，進士擢第，又應博學宏辭科。 元和末，累官至監察御史。 穆宗初即位，不修政道，盤遊無節，虞卿上疏諫曰：
Yuqing passed the jinshi examination and also entered the examination for erudite learning and grand rhetoric. By the end of the Yuanhe reign he had risen through successive promotions to imperial censor. When Emperor Muzong first came to the throne he neglected governance and wandered without restraint. Yuqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
29
臣聞鳶烏遭害則仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅則良言進。 況詔旨勉諭，許陳愚誠，故臣不敢避誅，以獻狂瞽。
I have heard that when birds of prey are harmed, virtuous birds depart; when slander goes unpunished, good counsel finds its way forward. Moreover, Your Majesty's edict encouraged frank speech and permitted humble sincerity; therefore I dare not shrink from reproof and offer these rash and blind words.
30
竊聞堯、舜受命，以天下為憂，不聞以位為樂。 況北虜猶梗，西戎未賓，兩河之瘡磐未平，五嶺之妖氛未解。 生人之疾苦盡在，朝廷之制度莫修，邊儲屢空，國用猶屈。 固未可以高枕無虞也。
I have heard that when Yao and Shun received Heaven's mandate, they worried for the realm and did not rejoice in the throne. Moreover, the northern tribes still resist, the western tribes have not submitted, the wounds of the two He regions are not yet healed, and unrest in the five Ling ranges is not yet settled. The people's suffering is everywhere; the court's institutions lie unreformed; frontier stores are repeatedly emptied; and state revenue is still strained. Surely one cannot rest easy and be free of care.
31
陛下初臨萬宇，有憂天下之志。 宜日延輔臣公卿百執事，凝旒而問，造膝以求，使四方內外，有所觀焉。 自聽政已來，六十日矣，八開延英，獨三數大臣仰龍顏，承聖問。 其餘侍從詔誥之臣，偕入而齊出，何足以聞政事哉！ 諫臣盈廷，忠言未聞於聖聽，臣實羞之。 蓋由主恩尚疏，而眾正之路未啟也。
When Your Majesty first faced the myriad realms, you had a mind to worry for the empire. You ought each day to receive your assisting ministers, nobles, and the hundred officials—listening attentively and questioning closely—so that all within and without may see and take heed. Since you began to hold court, sixty days have passed. Yanying Hall has opened eight times, yet only a few chief ministers have looked upon your countenance and received your questions. The rest—the attendants and edict drafters—enter together and leave together. How can they truly hear affairs of government? Remonstrance counselors fill the court, yet loyal words have not reached your ears—I am truly ashamed. Surely this is because your favor is still withheld and the path for upright counsel has not yet been opened.
32
夫公卿大臣，宜朝夕接見論道，賜與從容，則君臣之情相接，而理道備聞矣。 今自宰相已下四五人，時得頃刻侍坐，天威不遠，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來。 此由君太尊、臣太卑故也。 自公卿已下，雖歷踐清地，曾未祗奉天睠，以承下問，郁塞正路，偷安幸門。 況陛下神聖如五帝，臣下莫能望清光。 所宜周遍顧問，惠其氣色，使支體相輔，君臣喻明。 陛下求理於公卿，公卿求理於臣輩，自然上下孜孜相問，使進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤。 如此而不聞過失、不致升平者，未之有也。
High ministers and grand counselors ought to be received morning and evening to discuss the Way, granted unhurried conversation—then the bond between ruler and minister would be joined and the principles of governance fully heard. Now from the chief ministers downward, only four or five men at a time may sit in attendance for a brief moment. Your majesty is close at hand—they bow and tremble, rising and falling at your word, unable to speak freely with you. This happens because Your Majesty stands too far above your ministers, and they too far below you. From chief ministers downward, though they have repeatedly held honorable offices, they have never truly received your favor or answered your questions; the path of upright counsel is blocked, and they rest content at the gate of private advantage. Moreover, Your Majesty's sage virtue rivals that of the Five Emperors, and your officials cannot even meet your gaze. You ought to inquire of them widely and grant them unhurried audience, so that the whole body of government works as one and ruler and ministers understand each other clearly. If Your Majesty seeks good counsel from your chief ministers, and they in turn seek it from their subordinates, then naturally all ranks will diligently question one another, offering loyalty as eagerly as one pursues profit and debating policy as urgently as one pleads for justice. If matters stood thus and the throne still did not learn of its errors and the realm did not reach peace, it would be without precedent.
33
自古帝王，居危思安之心不相殊，而居安慮危之心不相及，故不得皆為聖帝明王。
Since ancient times, every ruler facing danger has wished for safety, but few who dwell in safety have thought ahead to danger; for this reason not all have become sage and enlightened sovereigns.
34
小臣疏賤，豈宜及此，獨不忍冒榮偷祿，以負聖朝。 惟陛下圖之。
I am humble and unworthy to speak of such things, yet I cannot bear to accept rank and salary in vain and fail this sacred dynasty. I beg Your Majesty to consider this.
35
帝深獎其言。 尋令奉使西北邊，犒賞戍卒，遷侍御史，再轉禮部員外郎、史館修撰。 八月，改吏部員外郎。
The emperor was deeply impressed by his memorial. Soon afterward he was sent as envoy to the northwest frontier to reward the garrison troops. He was promoted to supervising censor, then transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute. In the eighth month he was reassigned as assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.

，南曹令史李幹等六人，偽出告身簽符，賣鑿空偽官，令赴任者六十五人，取受錢一萬六千七百三十貫。 虞卿按得偽狀，捕幹等移御史臺鞫劾。 幹稱六人共率錢二千貫，與虞卿廳典溫亮，求不發舉偽濫事跡。 乃詔給事中嚴休復、中書舍人高鉞、左丞韋景休充三司推案，而溫亮逃竄。 幹等既伏誅，虞卿以檢下無術，停見任。
Six clerks of the South Bureau, including Li Gan, forged commission documents and seals and sold fraudulent appointments on the open market. Sixty-five men took up these bogus posts, paying a total of 16,730 strings of cash. Yuqing uncovered the fraud, arrested Gan and his accomplices, and had them transferred to the Censorate for trial. Gan claimed the six had pooled two thousand strings of cash and given them to Wen Liang, the chief clerk in Yuqing's office, in exchange for suppressing the investigation. An edict appointed Yan Xiufu, Gao Yue, and Wei Jingxiu to conduct a special commission of investigation, while Wen Liang fled. After Gan and his accomplices were executed, Yuqing was suspended from office for failing to supervise his staff properly.

及李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，起為左司郎中。 五年六月，拜諫議大夫，充弘文館學士，判院事。 六年，轉給事中。 七年，宗閔罷相，李德裕知政事，出為常州刺史。
When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru came to power, he was recalled as director in the Left Bureau. In the sixth month of the fifth year he was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor, made academician of the Hongwen Institute, and put in charge of its affairs. In the sixth year he was promoted to supervising secretary. In the seventh year, after Zongmin left office and Li Deyu assumed power, Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Changzhou.

虞卿性柔佞，能阿附權幸以為奸利。 每歲銓曹貢部，為舉選人馳走取科第，占員闕，無不得其所欲； 升沈取舍，出其脣吻。 而李宗閔待之如骨肉，以能朋比唱和，故時號黨魁。 八年，宗閔復入相，尋召為工部侍郎。 九年四月，拜京兆尹。 其年六月，京師訛言鄭註為上合金丹，須小兒心肝，密旨捕小兒無算。 民間相告語，扃鎖小兒甚密，街肆洶洶。 上聞之不悅，鄭註頗不自安。 御史大夫李固言素嫉虞卿朋黨，乃奏曰：「臣昨窮問其由，此語出於京兆尹從人，因此扇於都下。 」上怒，即令收虞卿下獄。 虞卿弟漢公並男知進等八人自系，撾鼓訴冤，詔虞卿歸私第。 翌日，貶虔州司馬，再貶虔州司戶，卒於貶所。
Yuqing was by nature supple and sycophantic, skilled at currying favor with the powerful for illicit gain. Each year during the selection and examination season he worked the appointments bureaucracy on behalf of candidates—securing ranks, claiming vacancies—always getting them what they wanted; Promotions, demotions, and appointments alike depended on his word. Li Zongmin treated him as family, and because he excelled at building factional alliances, he was known at the time as the leader of the clique. In the eighth year, when Zongmin returned as chief minister, Yuqing was soon recalled as vice minister of works. In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao. That June a rumor swept the capital that Zheng Zhu was compounding an elixir of immortality for the emperor and needed the hearts and livers of children; by secret order countless children were seized. Panicked whispers passed from house to house, parents locked their children indoors, and the streets seethed with alarm. When the emperor heard of this he was displeased, and Zheng Zhu grew deeply uneasy. Censor-in-Chief Li Guyan, who had long resented Yuqing's faction, memorialized: "Yesterday I pursued this to its source. The rumor originated with the metropolitan governor's attendants and was spread throughout the capital from there. " The emperor was furious and ordered Yuqing arrested at once. Yuqing's brother Han Gong and his sons, including Zhijin—eight men in all—bound themselves and beat the drum of appeal to protest his innocence. An edict then allowed Yuqing to return home. The next day he was demoted to army adjutant of Qianzhou, demoted again to registrar of the same prefecture, and died in exile.

子知進、知退、堪，弟漢公，皆登進士第。 知退歷都官、戶部二郎中； 堪庫部、吏部二員外郎。 虞卿弟漢公漢公，擢進士第，又書判拔萃，釋褐為李絳興元從事。 絳遇害，漢公遁而獲免。 累遷戶部郎中、史館修撰。 ，遷司封郎中。
His sons Zhijin, Zhihui, and Kan, together with his brother Han Gong, all passed the jinshi examination. Zhihui served successively as director in the Ministries of Justice and Revenue. Kan served as assistant director in the Treasury Department and the Ministry of Personnel. Yuqing's younger brother Han Gong passed the jinshi examination, distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination, and took his first post as a staff officer to Li Jiang at Xingyuan. When Li Jiang was murdered, Han Gong fled and survived. He rose in succession to director in the Ministry of Revenue and compiler at the Historiography Institute. He was then promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel for enfeoffments.
40
漢公子範、籌，皆登進士第，累辟使府。 虞卿從兄汝士虞卿從兄汝士。 汝士，字慕巢，進士擢第，又登博學宏詞科，累辟使府。 為右補闕。 坐弟殷士貢舉覆落，貶開江令。 入為戶部員外，再遷職方郎中。 七月，以本官知制誥。 時李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，待汝士厚。 尋正拜中書舍人，改工部侍郎。 八年，出為同州刺史。 九年九月，入為戶部侍郎。 七月，轉兵部侍郎。 其年十二月，檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。 時宗人嗣復鎮西川，兄弟對居節制，時人榮之。 四年九月，入為吏部侍郎，位至尚書，卒。
Han Gong's sons Fan and Chou both passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on commission staffs. Yuqing's elder cousin Ru Shi. Ru Shi, whose courtesy name was Muchao, passed the jinshi examination and the special erudite examination, and repeatedly served on commission staffs. He served as right supplements censor. Because his brother Yinshi was struck from the examination rolls upon re-examination, Ru Shi was demoted to magistrate of Kaijiang. He returned to court as assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue, then was promoted to director in the Ministry of War. In the seventh month he was given charge of drafting edicts while retaining his existing rank. At that time Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held power and treated Ru Shi with great favor. He was soon formally appointed vice director in the Secretariat and promoted to vice minister of works. In the eighth year he was sent out as prefect of Tongzhou. In the ninth month of the ninth year he returned to court as vice minister of revenue. In the seventh month he was transferred to vice minister of war. That December he was made acting minister of rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military governor of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan. At the time his clansman Sifu governed Western Chuan, so the two brothers held neighboring military commands—a distinction widely admired. In the ninth month of the fourth year he returned as vice minister of personnel, rose to minister, and died.
41
子知溫、知遠、知權，皆登進士第。 汝士子知溫知溫累官至禮部郎中、知制誥，入為翰林學士、戶部侍郎，轉左丞。 出為河南尹、陜虢觀察使。 遷檢校兵部尚書、襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。 知溫弟知至知溫弟知至，累官至比部郎中、知制誥。 坐故府劉瞻罷相，貶官。 知至亦貶瓊州司馬。 入為諫議大夫，累遷京兆尹、工部侍郎。 知溫、知至皆位至列曹尚書。 汝士弟魯士汝士弟魯士。 魯士，字宗尹，本名殷士。 ，進士擢第，其年詔翰林覆試。 殷士與鄭朗等覆落，因改名魯士。 復登制科，位不達而卒。
His sons Zhiwen, Zhiyuan, and Zhiquan all passed the jinshi examination. Ru Shi's son Zhiwen rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts, then entered court as Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue before becoming left vice director. He left the capital to serve as governor of Henan and commissioner of the Shan-Guo circuit. He was promoted to acting minister of war, prefect of Xiangzhou, and military governor of the Eastern Mountain-South circuit. Zhiwen's younger brother Zhizhi rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue for audits with charge of drafting edicts. When his former patron Liu Zhan was dismissed as chief minister, Zhizhi was demoted. Zhizhi was also demoted to army adjutant of Qiongzhou. He returned to court as remonstrance and policy advisor and eventually rose to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and vice minister of works. Both Zhiwen and Zhizhi rose to ministerial rank. Ru Shi's younger brother Lushi. Lushi, whose courtesy name was Zongyin, was originally named Yinshi. He passed the jinshi examination, but that same year the Hanlin Academy was ordered to re-examine the results. Yinshi, along with Zheng Lang and others, was struck from the rolls upon re-examination, after which he changed his name to Lushi. He passed a special decree examination but died without reaching high office.

初汝士中第，有時名，遂歷清貫。 其年諸子皆至正卿，郁為昌族。 所居靜恭里，知溫兄弟，並列門戟。 咸通中，昆仲子孫，在朝行方鎮者十餘人。 馬植馬植，扶風人。 父曛。 植，進士擢第，又登制策科，釋褐壽州團練副使。 得秘書省校書郎，三遷饒州刺史。 開成初，遷安南都護、御史中丞、安南招討使。
When Ru Shi first passed the examination he enjoyed wide renown and rose through a succession of prestigious posts. Within a generation his sons had all risen to high ministerial rank, making theirs a flourishing family. They lived in Jinggong Lane, where Zhiwen and his brothers all displayed the gate halberds of high office side by side. During the Xiantong era more than ten members of the family held posts at court or as regional governors. Ma Zhi—Ma Zhi was a native of Fufeng. His father was Xun. Zhi passed the jinshi and special policy examinations and took his first post as deputy military training commissioner of Shou Prefecture. He became a collator in the Secretariat and after three promotions was appointed prefect of Rao. Early in the Kaicheng era he was appointed protector-general of Annan, vice censor-in-chief, and pacification commissioner of Annan.

植文雅之餘，長於吏術。 三年，奏：「當管羈縻州首領，或居巢穴自固，或為南蠻所誘，不可招諭，事有可虞。 臣自到鎮，約之以信誠，曉之以逆順。 今諸首領，總發忠言，願納賦稅。 其武陸縣請升為州，以首領為刺史。 」從之。 又奏陸州界廢珠池復生珠。 以能政，就加檢校左散騎常侍，加中散大夫，轉黔中觀察使。 會昌中，入為大理卿。
In addition to his literary gifts he was accomplished in administrative skill. In the third year he memorialized: "The tribal chieftains of the subject prefectures under my jurisdiction either hold themselves in mountain strongholds or are being incited by the southern tribes; they cannot be won over by persuasion, and the situation is worrisome. Since I took up my post I have treated them with sincerity and made clear the consequences of loyalty and rebellion. Now all the chieftains have pledged their loyalty and offer to pay tribute and taxes. They request that Wulu County be elevated to prefectural status and that the chieftain be appointed its prefect. " The request was approved. He also reported that an abandoned pearl bed within Luzhou's territory was once again yielding pearls. In recognition of his capable administration he was given the additional title of acting left regular attendant, promoted to grand master of palace leisure, and transferred as commissioner of the Qianzhong circuit. During the Huichang era he returned to court as chief minister of justice.

植以文學政事為時所知。 久在邊遠，及還朝，不獲顯官，必微有望，李德裕素不重之。 宣宗即位，宰相白敏中與德裕有隙，凡德裕所薄者，必不次拔擢之。 乃加植金紫光祿大夫，行刑部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。 轉戶部侍郎，領使如故。 俄以本官同平章事，遷中書侍郎，兼禮部尚書。 敏中罷相，植亦罷為太子賓客，分司東都。 數年，出為許州刺史、檢校刑部尚書、忠武軍節度觀察等使。 大中末，遷汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使。 卒於鎮。 李讓夷李讓夷，字達心，隴西人。 祖悅，父應規。 讓夷，擢進士第，釋褐諸侯府。 太和初入朝，為右拾遺，召充翰林學士，轉左補闕。 三年，遷職方員外郎、左司郎中，充職。 九年，拜諫議大夫。
Zhi was renowned for his scholarship and administrative ability. After long service in remote regions, he returned to court without winning a prominent post; though he clearly hoped for one, Li Deyu had never held him in high regard. When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, chief minister Bai Minzhong, who feuded with Deyu, promoted out of turn everyone Deyu had looked down upon. Zhi was therefore made grand master of the gold seal and purple girdle, acting vice minister of justice, and commissioner for salt and iron transport. He was promoted to vice minister of revenue while continuing in his transport commission. He soon joined the chief council of state, was made vice director of the Secretariat, and concurrently minister of rites. When Minzhong left office, Zhi was also dismissed and given the nominal post of mentor to the heir apparent in the Eastern Capital. Several years later he was sent out as prefect of Xu, acting minister of justice, and military governor of the Zhongwu Army. Late in the Dazhong era he was transferred to prefect of Bian and military governor of the Xuanwu Army. He died in office. Li Rangyi—Li Rangyi, whose courtesy name was Daxin, was a native of Longxi. His grandfather was Yue; his father was Yinggui. Rangyi passed the jinshi examination and, upon leaving probationary service, took his first appointment on a regional lord's staff. Early in the Tahe era he entered court service, was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor of the right, was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, and was transferred to left supplementation censor. In the third year he was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Appointments and left department director, continuing in both posts. In the ninth year he was appointed remonstrance and policy advisor.
45
，以本官兼知起居舍人事。 時起居舍人李褒有痼疾，請罷官。 宰臣李石奏闕官，上曰：「褚遂良為諫議大夫，嘗兼此官，卿可盡言今諫議大夫姓名。 」石遂奏李讓夷、馮定、孫簡、蕭俶。 帝曰：「讓夷可也。 」李固言欲用崔球、張次宗。 鄭覃曰：「崔球遊宗閔之門，赤墀下秉筆記註，為千古法，不可用朋黨。 如裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有纖芥異論。 」其為人主大臣知重如此。 二年，拜中書舍人。 以鄭覃此言，深為李玨、楊嗣復所惡，終文宗世，官不達。
He also took charge of the diarist office while retaining his existing rank. At the time the diarist Li Bao suffered from a chronic illness and asked to resign. Chief Minister Li Shi reported the vacancy. The emperor said, "When Chu Suiliang served as remonstrance and policy advisor, he once also held this office. Report fully the names of the current remonstrance and policy advisors. " Li Shi then nominated Li Rangyi, Feng Ding, Sun Jian, and Xiao Shu. The emperor said, "Rangyi will do. " Li Guyen wanted to appoint Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong. Zheng Tan said, "Cui Qiu moves in Li Zongmin's circle. Recording and annotating below the red steps of the throne hall is a precedent for all ages; one must not appoint men from partisan factions. As for men such as Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, I would not venture the slightest objection. " Such was the esteem in which rulers and chief ministers held him. In the second year he was appointed drafting secretary of the central secretariat. Because of Zheng Tan's remark, he was deeply resented by Li Jue and Yang Sifu, and throughout Emperor Wenzong's reign he never advanced far in office.
46
及德裕秉政，驟加拔擢，歷工、戶二侍郎，轉左丞。 累遷檢校尚書右僕射，俄拜中書侍郎，同平章事。 宣宗即位罷相，以太子賓客分司卒。 魏謩魏謩，字申之，鉅鹿人。 五代祖文貞公徵，貞觀朝名相。 曾祖殷，汝陽令。 祖明，亦為縣令。 父馮，獻陵臺令。 謩，登進士第。 楊汝士牧同州，辟為防禦判官，得秘書省校書郎。 汝士入朝，薦為右拾遺。 文宗以謩魏徵之裔，頗奇待之。
When Li Deyu came to power, he was suddenly elevated, serving successively as vice minister of works and vice minister of revenue, then as left vice director. He rose in succession to acting right vice director of the department of state affairs, and soon after was appointed vice director of the central secretariat and co-equal chief minister. When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was removed from the chancellorship and died while serving as guest of the crown prince in a supervisory post at Luoyang. Wei Mo—Wei Mo, whose courtesy name was Shenzhi, was a native of Julu. His fifth-generation ancestor, Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng, had been a famous chief minister in the Zhenguan reign. His great-grandfather Yin had been magistrate of Ruyang. His grandfather Ming had also served as a county magistrate. His father Feng had been director of the Xianling platform. Mo passed the jinshi examination. When Yang Rushi served as governor of Tong Prefecture, he recruited Mo as defense staff judge and secured for him the post of collator in the Secretariat. When Rushi came to court, he recommended Mo as remonstrance and policy advisor of the right. Emperor Wenzong, knowing Mo to be a descendant of Wei Zheng, treated him with special regard.
47
前邕管經略使董昌齡枉殺錄事參軍衡方厚，坐貶漵州司戶。 至是量移硤州刺史，謩上疏論之曰：「王者施渙汗之恩以赦有罪，唯故意殺人無赦。 昌齡比者錄以微效，授之方隅，不能祗慎寵光，恣其狂暴，無辜專殺，事跡顯彰。 妻孥銜冤，萬里披訴。 及按鞫伏罪，貸以微生，中外議論，以為屈法。 今若授之牧守，以理疲人，則殺人者拔擢，而冤苦者何伸？ 交紊憲章，有乘至理。 」疏奏，乃改為洪州別駕。
Formerly the military governor of the Yong-Guan circuit, Dong Changling, had unjustly executed registrar Heng Fanghou and was demoted to registrar of Xuzhou. At this point he was transferred to governor of Xia Prefecture. Mo submitted a memorial arguing against the appointment, saying, "A ruler grants sweeping clemency to forgive the guilty, but deliberate homicide is never forgiven. Changling was recently noted for minor merit and given a frontier post, yet failed to honor the imperial favor with due reverence, indulging his violence and killing the innocent at will—the facts are plain. His wife and children nursed their grievance and traveled ten thousand li to plead their case. When investigation proved his guilt, he was spared with only a light punishment, and both court and country regarded it as a bending of the law. If he is now given a governorship to rule over a weary populace, then the killer is promoted—how can the wronged obtain redress? This would entangle and disorder the statutes and violate fundamental principle. " When the memorial was submitted, the appointment was changed to vice prefect of Hong Prefecture.
