御史中丞李孝本，皇族也，坐李訓誅，有女沒人掖廷。 謩諫曰：
Vice censor-in-chief Li Xiaoben, a member of the imperial clan, was implicated in Li Xun's execution, and his daughter was taken into the palace women's quarters. Mo remonstrated, saying:
49
臣聞治國家者，先資於德義； 德義不修，家邦必壞。 故王者以德服人，以義使人。 服使之術，要在修身； 修身之道，在於孜孜。 夫一失百虧之戒，存乎久要之源。 前志曰：「勿以小惡而為之，勿以小善而不為。 」斯則懼於漸也！ 臣又聞，君如日焉，顯晦之微，人皆瞻仰； 照臨之大，何以掩藏？ 前代設敢諫之鼓，立誹謗之木，貴聞其過也。 陛下即位以來，誕敷文德，不悅聲色，出後宮之怨婦，配在外之鰥夫。 洎今十年，未嘗采擇。 自數月已來，天睠稍回，留神妓樂，教坊百人、二百人，選試未已； 莊宅司收市，亹癖有聞。 昨又宣取李孝本之女入內。 宗姓不異，寵幸何名？ 此事深累慎修，有虧一簣。 陛下九重之內，不得聞知。 凡此之流，大生物議，實傷理道之本，未免塵穢之嫌。 夫欲人不知，莫若勿為。 諺曰：「止寒莫若重裘，止謗莫若自修。 」伏希陛下照鑒不惑； 崇千載之盛德，去一旦之玩好。 教坊停息，宗女遣還，則大正人倫之風，深弘王者之體。
"I have heard that those who govern a state must first rely upon virtue and righteousness; if virtue and righteousness are not cultivated, the family and realm will surely fall to ruin. Therefore the ruler makes men submit through virtue and moves them through righteousness. The art of winning submission and service lies in self-cultivation; the way of self-cultivation lies in unceasing effort. The warning that one fault may undo a hundred accomplishments rests in the root of constancy over the long term. Former writings say: 'Do not do what is evil though it be small; do not fail to do what is good though it be small. ' This is to guard against the gradual slide! I have also heard that the ruler is like the sun—whether bright or dim, the slightest change, all men observe; the breadth of his illumination—how can it be concealed? Former dynasties set up drums for bold remonstrance and poles for posting criticism, valuing the hearing of their faults. Since Your Majesty's accession you have spread civil virtue abroad, taken no pleasure in music and women, released wronged women from the inner palace, and matched them in marriage to widowers outside. Down to the present, ten years on, you have never taken selections from the palace. Since several months ago Heaven's favor has shifted slightly—you have turned your attention to performers, and a hundred or two hundred from the Academy of Music have been selected and tested without cease; the Palatial Estates Office has been buying up properties, and your special fondnesses have become known. Yesterday the order went out to bring Li Xiaoben's daughter into the inner palace. She shares the imperial surname—what name can be given to favoring her? This affair deeply undermines careful self-cultivation and falls short by a basketful of earth at the end of a mound. Within the innermost palace, Your Majesty did not hear of it. Such conduct greatly provokes public criticism, truly injures the foundation of moral order, and cannot escape the taint of scandal. If one wishes that others not know, there is nothing better than not doing it. As the proverb says: 'To stop cold, nothing is better than a heavy fur; to stop slander, nothing is better than self-reform. ' I humbly hope Your Majesty will examine this without confusion; uphold your everlasting great virtue and set aside a moment's indulgence. If the Academy of Music is halted and the clanswoman sent back, then the moral order will be greatly rectified and the dignity of kingship deeply affirmed.
50
疏奏，帝即日出孝本女，遷謩右補闕。 詔曰：「昔乃先祖貞觀中諫書十上，指事直言，無所避諱。 每覽國史，未嘗不沈吟伸卷，嘉尚久之。 爾為拾遺，其風不墜，屢獻章疏，必道其所以。 至於備灑掃於諸王，非自廣其聲妓也； 恤髫齔之宗女，固無嫌於徵取也。 雖然，疑似之間，不可家至而戶曉。 爾能詞旨深切，是博我之意多也。 噫！ 人能匪躬謇諤，似其先祖； 吾豈不能虛懷延納，仰希貞觀之理歟？ 而謩居官日淺，未當敘進，吾豈限以常典，以待直臣！ 可右補闕。 」帝謂宰臣曰：「昔太宗皇帝得魏徵，裨補闕失，弼成聖政。 我得魏謩，於疑似之間，必能極諫。 不敢希貞觀之政，庶幾處無過之地矣。 」
When the memorial was submitted, the emperor released Li Xiaoben's daughter that same day and promoted Mo to right supplementation censor. An edict said, "In former times your ancestor in the Zhenguan era submitted ten memorials of remonstrance, speaking directly to the matter at hand without evasion. Each time I read the national histories, I have never failed to pause in contemplation and unfold the scroll, admiring him at length. You serve as remonstrance and policy advisor; his spirit has not fallen. You have repeatedly submitted memorials, always stating your reasons. As for training performers for the princes' households, this was not to enlarge your own troupe of musicians; in taking pity on a clanswoman still in childhood, there was naturally no impropriety in bringing her in. Even so, in matters of suspicion and appearance, one cannot make every household understand. You were able to make your words deeply felt—that shows how much you broadened my understanding. Alas! When a man can disregard himself and speak forthrightly, he resembles his ancestor; can I not open my heart and welcome remonstrance, looking up to the governance of the Zhenguan era? Yet Mo's time in office has been brief and he is not yet due for promotion—shall I be bound by ordinary precedent when rewarding an upright minister! He may be appointed right supplementation censor. " The emperor said to his chief ministers, "Formerly Emperor Taizong gained Wei Zheng, who remedied oversights and deficiencies and helped bring about sagely governance. I have gained Wei Mo—at the brink of doubtful appearances, he is sure to remonstrate to the utmost. I dare not hope for the governance of Zhenguan, yet perhaps I may stand where there is no fault. "
51
教坊副使雲朝霞善吹笛，新聲變律，深愜上旨。 自左驍衛將軍宣授兼揚府司馬。 宰臣奏曰：「揚府司馬品高，郎官刺史叠處，不可授伶官。 」上意欲授之，因宰臣對，亟稱朝霞之善。 謩聞之，累疏陳論，乃改授潤州司馬。 荊南監軍使呂令琮從人，擅入江陵縣，毀罵縣令韓忠，觀察使韋長申狀與樞密使訴之。 謩上疏曰：「伏以州縣侵屈，只合上聞。 中外關連，須存舊制。 韋長任膺廉使，體合精詳，公事都不奏聞，私情擅為逾越。 況事無巨細，不可將迎。 縣令官業有乖，便宜理罪； 監軍職司侵越，即合聞天。 或以慮煩聖聽，何不但申門下？ 今則首紊常典，理合糾繩。 伏望聖慈，速加懲戒！ 」疏奏不出，時論惜之。
Deputy director of the Academy of Music Yun Zhaoxia was skilled at playing the flute, inventing new melodies and altering modes, deeply pleasing the emperor's taste. By direct imperial order he was promoted from left Xiaowei army general to serve concurrently as military aide of Yang Prefecture. The chief ministers reported, "The military aide of Yang Prefecture is a high-ranking post occupied in turn by palace gentlemen and prefects—it must not be granted to a performer. " The emperor wished to grant it, and in response to the chief ministers repeatedly praised Zhaoxia's excellence. When Mo heard of this, he submitted memorial after memorial arguing against it, and Zhaoxia was instead appointed military aide of Run Prefecture. A retainer of Jingnan military commissioner Lü Lingcong entered Jiangling County without authorization, reviled and cursed the magistrate Han Zhong, and the observation commissioner Wei Chang submitted a report to the commissioner of military affairs to lodge a complaint. Mo submitted a memorial saying, "It is submitted that when prefectures and counties suffer encroachment and injustice, reports should ascend only to the throne. Links between the inner and outer courts must preserve the former institutions. Wei Chang holds the post of integrity commissioner and ought in principle to be thorough and precise, yet he did not report the official matter and on private grounds overstepped by petitioning the military affairs commissioner. Moreover, whether matters are great or small, one must not curry favor. If a county magistrate's official conduct is at fault, he should be punished according to law; if a military commissioner oversteps his duties, that should be reported to the throne. If one fears burdening the sacred ear, why not report only to the Secretariat? As it stands, he has first disrupted regular precedent and should be called to account. I humbly hope Your Sacred Benevolence will swiftly impose punishment! " When the memorial was submitted it was not issued, and public opinion deplored it.
52
三年，轉起居舍人。 紫宸中謝，帝謂之曰：「以卿論事忠切，有文貞之風，故不循月限，授卿此官。 」又謂之曰：「卿家有何舊書詔？ 」對曰：「比多失墜，惟簪笏見存。 」上令進來。 鄭覃曰：「在人不在笏。 」上曰：「鄭覃不會我意，此即《甘棠》之義，非在笏而已。 」謩將退，又召誡之曰：「事有不當，即須奏論。 」謩曰：「臣頃為諫官，合伸規諷。 今居史職，職在記言，臣不敢輒逾職分。 」帝曰：「凡兩省官並合論事，勿拘此言。 」尋以本官直弘文館。
In the third year he was transferred to diarist. At his thanksgiving audience in the Purple Glazed Hall, the emperor said to him, "Because your remonstrance is loyal and earnest and carries the spirit of Duke Wen Zhen, I grant you this office without waiting for the monthly term limit. " He also said to him, "What old imperial writings and edicts does your family possess? " He replied, "Many have been lost over time; only the court cap and ivory tablet remain. " The emperor ordered them brought in. Zheng Tan said, "Honor rests with the man, not with the ivory tablet. " The emperor said, "Zheng Tan misses my point. This is the lesson of the Sweet Pear Tree—it is not about the tablet alone. " As Mo was about to leave, the emperor called him back and warned him, "Whenever something is wrong, you must speak up in memorial at once. " Mo said, "I was recently a remonstrance official, and it was my duty to offer frank counsel and pointed remonstrance. Now I serve as a historiographer, and my duty is to record what is said. I dare not overstep my role on my own authority. " The emperor said, "Officials in both secretariats should all discuss state affairs. Do not hold yourself to that limit. " He was soon assigned to serve at the Hongwen Academy while retaining his existing post.
53
四年，拜諫議大夫，仍兼起居舍人，判弘文館事。 紫宸入閣，遣中使取謩起居註，欲視之。 謩執奏曰：「自古置史官，書事以明鑒誡。 陛下但為善事，勿畏臣不書。 如陛下所行錯忤，臣縱不書，天下之人書之。 臣以陛下為文皇帝，陛下比臣如褚遂良。 」帝又曰：「我嘗取觀之。 」謩曰：「由史官不守職分，臣豈敢陷陛下為非法？ 陛下一覽之後，自此書事須有回避。 如此，善惡不直，非史也。 遺後代，何以取信？ 」乃止。
In the fourth year he was made remonstrance grand master, retained his post as diarist, and was put in charge of the Hongwen Academy. During an audience in the Purple Glazed Hall, the emperor sent a palace envoy to fetch Mo's court diary, intending to read it. Mo stood firm and replied, "Historiographers have existed since antiquity precisely so that events may be recorded as a clear mirror and a warning. If Your Majesty does only what is right, you need never worry that I will leave it unrecorded. If Your Majesty acts wrongly, even if I fail to record it, the world will still write it down. I regard Your Majesty as another Emperor Wen; I ask only that you treat me as you would Chu Suiliang. " The emperor added, "I have looked at such records before. " Mo said, "Those historiographers failed in their duty. How could I allow Your Majesty to be drawn into what the law forbids? Once you have read the record, everything written thereafter will be shaped by what you are allowed to see. If that happens, right and wrong will no longer be written plainly, and the record will cease to be history. How could future generations ever trust such a record? " With that, the emperor dropped the matter.
54
初立朝，為李固言、李玨、楊嗣復所引，數年之內，至諫議大夫。 武宗即位，李德裕用事，謩坐楊、李之黨，出為汾州刺史。 楊、李貶官，謩亦貶信州長史。 宣宗即位，白敏中當國，量移郢州刺史，尋換商州。 二年，內徵為給事中，遷御史中丞。 謝日，面賜金紫之服。 彈駙馬都尉杜中立贓罪，貴戚憚之。 兼戶部侍郎，判本司事。 謩奏曰：「御史臺紀綱之地，不宜與泉貨吏雜處，乞罷中司，專綜戶部公事。 」從之。
When he first took office, he was promoted by Li Guyen, Li Jue, and Yang Sifu, and within a few years reached the rank of remonstrance grand master. When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Li Deyu dominated the government. Mo, counted among the Yang and Li faction, was posted out as prefect of Fenzhou. When Yang and Li were stripped of their offices, Mo was demoted as well, to chief administrator of Xinzhou. When Emperor Xuanzong came to power and Bai Minzhong took control of the government, Mo was moved laterally to prefect of Yingzhou and soon transferred to Shangzhou. In the second year he was recalled to court as supervising secretary and then promoted to vice-director of the censorate. On the day of his audience of thanks, the emperor personally bestowed on him the gold-and-purple robes of high rank. He impeached Du Zhongli, commandant-in-chief of horsemen and an imperial son-in-law, on charges of corruption, and even powerful clansmen were wary of him. He was made vice minister of revenue as well and placed in charge of that ministry's business. Mo memorialized, "The censorate is the seat of institutional discipline. It should not be blended with the clerks who handle coin and grain. I ask to be relieved of the vice-directorship so I may devote myself wholly to revenue affairs. " The emperor agreed.
55
尋以本官同平章事，判使如故。 謝日，奏曰：「臣無夔、契之才，驟叨夔、契之任，將何以仰報鴻私？ 今邊戍粗安，海內寧息，臣愚所切者，陛下未立東宮，俾正人傳導，以存副貳之重。 」因泣下。 上感而聽之。
He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, and his other commissions remained the same. At his thanksgiving audience he memorialized, "I lack the wisdom of ministers such as Kui and Xie, yet I have suddenly been given a burden worthy of them. How can I ever repay Your Majesty's great kindness? The frontiers are calm and the realm is at peace. What weighs most on my mind is that Your Majesty has not yet named a crown prince and put upright mentors in the Eastern Palace to safeguard the institution of succession. " He broke down in tears as he spoke. The emperor was deeply moved and took his advice.
56
先是，累朝人君不欲人言立儲貳，若非人主己欲，臣下不敢獻言。 宣宗春秋高，嫡嗣未辨，謩作相之日，率先啟奏，人士重之。 尋兼集賢大學士。 詹毗國獻象，謩以其性不安中土，請還其使，從之。 太原節度使李業殺降虜，北邊大擾。 業有所恃，人不敢非。 謩即奏其事，乃移業滑州。 加中書侍郎。 大理卿馬曙從人王慶告曙家藏兵甲。 曙坐貶官，而慶無罪。 謩引法律論之，竟杖殺慶。
For generations, emperors had been unwilling to hear talk of naming an heir. Unless the ruler himself wished it, courtiers did not dare raise the subject. Emperor Xuanzong was growing old, and the succession had not yet been settled. The day Wei Mo took office as chancellor, he was the first to raise the issue openly, and the court admired him for it. He soon became a grand academician of the Jixian Academy as well. When the kingdom of Zhanbi sent an elephant as tribute, Mo argued that the creature could not thrive in the central lands and asked that the envoys be sent home. The court agreed. Li Ye, military commissioner of Taiyuan, executed prisoners who had surrendered, and the north erupted in turmoil. Li Ye enjoyed powerful patronage, and no one dared speak against him. Mo promptly memorialized on the affair, and Li Ye was reassigned to Huazhou. He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat. Ma Shu, chief judge of the court of judicial review, was accused by his retainer Wang Qing of hoarding arms and armor at home. Shu was found guilty and demoted, while Qing went unpunished. Mo invoked the law in memorial and ultimately had Qing beaten to death.
57
進階銀青光祿大夫，兼禮部尚書、監修國史。 修成《文宗實錄》四十卷，上之。 其修史官給事中盧耽、太常少卿蔣偕、司勛員外郎王諷、右補闕盧告、膳部員外郎牛叢，皆頒賜錦彩、銀器，序遷職秩。 謩轉門下侍郎，兼戶部尚書。 ，以本官平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使知節度事。 十一年，以疾求代，徵拜吏部尚書。 以疾未痊，乞授散秩，改檢校右僕射，守太子少保。 十二年十二月卒，時年六十六，贈司徒。
He was promoted to grand master of glorious affairs with silver-blue insignia and made minister of rites while supervising the compilation of the national history. He finished the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong in forty scrolls and presented them to the throne. The officials who had helped compile it—Lu Dan, Jiang Xie, Wang Feng, Lu Gao, and Niu Cong—were all rewarded with brocade silks and silver vessels and promoted in turn. Mo was moved to vice director of the chancellery and made minister of revenue as well. He was also appointed co-chancellor, prefect of Chengdu, and deputy commissioner of the Jiannan West circuit, with full authority over the circuit's military affairs. In the eleventh year he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness and was recalled as minister of personnel. Because he had not yet recovered, he asked for a purely honorary appointment and was made honorary right vice director of the department of state, serving as guardian crown prince junior tutor. He died in the twelfth month of the twelfth year at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of education.
58
謩儀容魁偉，言論切直，與同列上前言事，他宰相必委曲規諷，唯謩讜言無所畏避。 宣宗每曰：「魏謩綽有祖風，名公子孫，我心重之。 」然竟以語辭太剛，為令狐綯所忌，罷之。
Wei Mo cut an imposing figure and spoke with blunt directness. When he and his fellow chancellors addressed the throne, the others usually couched their advice in roundabout terms, but Mo alone spoke with fearless, uncompromising candor. Emperor Xuanzong often said, "Wei Mo truly inherits his family's legacy. As the son of a great house, he has my deep respect. " In the end, however, his blunt speech earned the resentment of Linghu Tao, and he was dismissed.
59
謩嘗鈔撮子書要言，以類相從，二十卷，號曰《魏氏手略》。 有文集十卷。
Wei Mo once compiled essential passages from various books, grouped them by subject into twenty scrolls, and called the work Hand Compendium of the Wei Clan. He also left a collected writings in ten scrolls.
60
子潛、滂。 潛登進士第。 潛子敖，韋琮甥。 後琮為相，潛歷顯官。 周墀周墀，字德升，汝南人。 祖颋，父霈。 墀，擢進士第，太和末，累遷至起居郎。 墀能為古文，有史才。 文宗重之，補集賢學士，轉考功員外郎，仍兼起居舍人事。 冬，以本官知制誥，尋召充翰林學士。 三年，遷職方郎中。 四年十月，正拜中書舍人，內職如故。 武宗即位，出為華州刺史、鎮國軍潼關防禦等使，改鄂州刺史、御史中丞、鄂嶽觀察使。 十一月，遷洪州刺史、江南西道觀察使。 大中初，檢校禮部尚書、滑州刺史、義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察等使、上柱國、汝南男，食邑三百戶。 入朝為兵部侍郎、判度支。 尋以本官同平章事，累遷銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、監修國史，兼刑部尚書。 罷相，檢校刑部尚書、梓州刺史、御史大夫、劍南東川節度使。 未行，追制改檢校右僕射，加食邑五百戶。 歷方鎮卒。 崔龜從崔龜從，字玄告，清河人。 祖璜，父誠，官微。 龜從，擢進士第，又登賢良方正制科，及書判拔萃二科，釋褐拜右拾遺。 ，改太常博士。
He had two sons, Qian and Pang. Qian passed the jinshi civil service examination. Qian's son Ao was the nephew of Wei Cong. When Cong later rose to chancellor, Qian advanced through a series of high offices. Zhou Chi—whose courtesy name was Desheng—was a native of Runan. His grandfather was Zhou Feng and his father Zhou Pei. Chi passed the jinshi examination, and by the end of the Taihe reign he had risen through repeated promotions to palace diarist. Chi wrote well in the ancient prose style and showed real talent as a historian. Emperor Wenzong valued him, made him an academician of the Jixian Academy, then promoted him to an outer-section officer in the ministry of personnel while keeping his duties as diarist. That winter he was assigned to draft imperial edicts while retaining his existing post, and was soon appointed a Hanlin academician. In the third year he was promoted to director of the bureau of appointments. In the tenth month of the fourth year he was formally made secretariat drafter while retaining his inner-court posts. When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, he was posted out as prefect of Huazhou and commissioner for the Zhenguo army and Tong Pass defenses, then transferred to prefect of Ezhou, vice-director of the censorate, and observer of E and Yue. In the eleventh month he was moved to prefect of Hongzhou and observer of the Jiangnan West circuit. Early in the Dazhong era he was made honorary minister of rites, prefect of Huazhou, military commissioner of the Yicheng army, and observer of Zheng and Hua circuits, with the titles upper pillar of the state and baron of Runan, enfeoffed with three hundred households. He was recalled to court as vice minister of war and put in charge of fiscal affairs. He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, then rose through successive promotions to grand master of glorious affairs with silver-blue insignia, vice director of the secretariat, supervisor of the national history, and minister of punishments. After leaving the chancellorship he was made honorary minister of punishments, prefect of Zizhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Jiannan East Sichuan circuit. Before he could take up the post, a follow-up edict reassigned him as honorary right vice director of the department of state and raised his enfeoffment by five hundred households. He ended his career in regional commands and died there. Cui Guicong—whose courtesy name was Xuangao—was a native of Qinghe. His grandfather was Cui Huang and his father Cui Cheng, both men of modest rank. Guicong passed the jinshi examination, then the special decree examination for worthy and upright candidates, and also the document-judgment and outstanding-selection examinations. On entering official service he was appointed right collector of remonstrance. He was soon transferred to erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices.
61
龜從長於禮學，精歷代沿革，問無不通。 時饗宗廟於敬宗室，祝板稱皇帝孝弟。 龜從議曰：「臣審祥孝字，載考禮文，義本主於子孫，理難施於兄弟。 按《禮記》卜虞之文，子孫曰哀，兄弟曰某。 然則虞之稱哀，與祭之稱孝，其義一也。 於祖禰則理宜稱孝，於伯仲則止可稱名。 又東晉溫嶠議宗廟祝辭，於孝字非子者則不稱，傍親直言敢告。 當時朝議，咸以為宜。 今臣上考禮經，無兄弟稱孝之義； 下徵晉史，有不稱傍親之文。 臣謂饗敬宗廟，宜去孝弟兩字。 」
Guicong was a master of ritual studies and knew the evolution of institutions across dynasties in meticulous detail. There was almost nothing in the field he could not explain. At the time, when sacrifices were offered in the ancestral temple at Emperor Jingzong's spirit tablet, the invocation addressed the emperor as "filial brother." Guicong argued, "I have examined the characters xiang and xiao against the ritual canon. Their meaning applies properly to descendants, not to brothers. The Book of Rites says that in the divination for the Yu rite, descendants are addressed as "ai" (the mournful), while brothers are addressed by personal name alone. In the same way, the term "ai" used at the Yu rite and "xiao" used at the sacrifice ceremony express the same underlying principle. Toward grandfathers and fathers it is proper to speak of filial devotion, but toward elder and younger brothers one may use only a personal name. Wen Jiao of the Eastern Jin likewise argued that in ancestral temple invocations the word xiao should not be used except by a son, and that collateral relatives should address the spirit directly with "I dare report." The court at the time unanimously agreed that this was correct. When I turn to the ritual classics, I find no precedent for brothers to use the word xiao; and when I consult Jin historical records, I find passages that likewise avoid addressing collateral relatives in that way. I therefore hold that in the sacrifice at Emperor Jingzong's temple, the words "filial brother" should be removed. "
62
又以祀九宮壇，舊是大祠。 龜從議曰：「九宮貴神，經典不載。 天寶中，術士奏請，遂立祠壇。 事出一時，禮同郊祀。 臣詳其圖法，皆主星名，縱司水旱兵荒，品秩不過列宿。 今者，五星悉是從祀，日月猶在中祠，豈容九宮獨越常禮，備列王事，誡誓百官？ 尊卑乖儀，莫甚於此。 若以嘗在祀典，不可廢除，臣請降為中祠。 」制從之。
He also weighed in on the sacrifice at the Nine Palaces altar, which had long been treated as a major state rite. Guicong argued, "The exalted spirits of the Nine Palaces are nowhere mentioned in the canonical classics. During the Tianbao reign, occult specialists petitioned for its establishment, and a sacrificial altar was duly built. It was a product of its moment, yet it was accorded the rites of a suburban sacrifice. On examination, the charts and formulae all name ordinary stars of the firmament. Even if they are said to govern flood, drought, war, and famine, their rank is no higher than the regular constellations. Today even the Five Planets are offered only as secondary sacrifices, and the sun and moon remain at the level of medium rites. How can the Nine Palaces alone be allowed to overstep ordinary precedent, take on the full trappings of a royal ceremony, and impose sworn admonitions upon the entire bureaucracy? Nothing could violate the proper order of high and low more grossly than this. If it cannot be abolished because it was once entered in the sacrificial canon, I ask that it be reduced to a medium sacrifice. " The emperor approved the proposal.
63
龜從又以大臣薨謝，不於聞哀日輟朝，奏議曰：「伏以廢朝軫悼，義重君臣，所貴及哀，尤宜示信。 自頃已來，輟朝非奏報之時，備禮於數日外。 雖遵常制，似不本情。 臣不敢遠徵古書，請引國朝故事：貞觀中任瑰卒，有司對仗奏闕聞，太宗責其乖禮； 岑文本既歿，其夕為罷警嚴； 張公謹之亡，哭之不避辰日。 是知閔悼之意，不宜過時。 臣謂大臣薨，禮合輟朝。 縱有機務急速，便殿須召宰臣，不臨正朝，無爽事體。 如此，則由衷之信，載感於幽明； 稱情之文，無虧於典禮。 」又奏：「文武三品官薨卒輟朝。 有未經親重之官，今任又是散列者，為之變禮，誠恐非宜。 自今後，文武三品以上官，非曾任將相，及曾在密近，宜加恩禮者，餘請不在輟朝之限。 」從之。
Guicong again addressed the court practice of acknowledging a great minister's death without suspending audience on the day the mourning news arrived. He submitted a memorial: "I humbly submit that suspending court to grieve carries the full weight of the bond between ruler and minister. The point is to respond while grief is fresh, and above all to act in good faith. In recent practice, court has not been suspended when the news was first reported, and the full mourning observances have been held days afterward. Though it follows established precedent, it hardly seems true to the heart of the matter. I will not reach back to remote antiquity, but cite our own dynasty's precedents: in the Zhenguan reign, when Ren Gui died, the responsible offices reported the lapse at imperial audience, and Emperor Taizong rebuked them for violating proper rite; when Cen Wenben died, the palace guard was suspended that very evening; when Zhang Gongjin died, the court mourned him without observing the Branch Day restrictions. This shows that sincere grief ought not to be delayed past its proper moment. I hold that when a great minister dies, ritual propriety requires suspending court. Even if urgent business required summoning the chief ministers to the side hall rather than holding formal audience, the substance of governance would remain intact. Done this way, genuine sincerity would move both the living and the dead; and the language of the rites would honor both feeling and canonical precedent. " He also submitted: "When a civil or military official of the third rank dies, court is suspended. To alter court ritual for officials who were never close to the throne, and who hold only perfunctory posts, would truly be inappropriate. Henceforth, only third-rank civil and military officials who formerly served as generals or chancellors, or who had served in close attendance and merited special honors, should qualify for court suspension; all others should be excluded. " The emperor approved.
64
累轉考功郎中、史館修撰。 九年，轉司勛郎中、知制誥。 十二月，正拜中書舍人。 開成初，出為華州刺史。 三年三月，人為戶部侍郎，判本司事。 四年，權判吏部尚書銓事。 ，為中書侍郎、同平章事，兼吏部尚書。 五年七月，撰成《續唐歷》三十卷，上之。 六年，罷相，檢校吏部尚書，汴州刺史、宣武軍節度觀察等使，累歷方鎮卒。 鄭肅鄭肅，滎陽人。 祖烈，父閱，世儒家。 肅苦心力學。 ，擢進士第，又以書判拔萃，歷佐使府。 太和初，入朝為尚書郎。 六年，轉太常少卿。 肅能為古文，長於經學，左丘明、《三禮》、儀註疑議，博士以下必就肅決之。
He rose through successive promotions to director in the ministry of personnel's examinations bureau and compiler at the Historiography Institute. In the ninth year he was made director in the ministry of personnel's merit-records bureau and assigned to draft imperial edicts. That December he received formal appointment as a secretariat drafter. Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as prefect of Huazhou. In the third month of the third year he was recalled to court as vice minister of revenue with charge of the ministry. In the fourth year he was given acting charge of the minister of personnel's selection examinations. He was appointed vice director of the secretariat, co-chancellor, and concurrently minister of personnel. In the seventh month of the fifth year he completed the thirty-scroll Continuation of the Tang Calendar and presented it to the throne. In the sixth year he left the chancellorship, became honorary minister of personnel, prefect of Bianzhou and military commissioner of the Xuanwu army, served through several regional postings, and died in office. Zheng Su was a native of Xingyang. His grandfather Lie and his father Yue were scholars; the family had produced Confucian scholars for generations. Su applied himself to study with tireless discipline. He passed the jinshi examination, distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination, and served on the staffs of several commissioners. Early in the Taihe reign he entered court service as a director in the department of state affairs. In the sixth year he was made vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices. Su wrote well in the ancient prose style and was deeply versed in the classics. On Zu Qiuming, the Three Rites, and disputed points in ritual commentaries, even court erudites routinely sought his judgment.
65
時魯王永有寵，文宗擇名儒為其府屬，用戶部侍郎庾敬休兼王傅，戶部郎中李踐方兼司馬，以肅本官兼長史，由是知名。 明年，魯王為太子，肅加給事中。 九年，改刑部侍郎，尋改尚書右丞，權判吏部西銓事。 開成初，出為陜虢都防禦觀察使、兼御史大夫。 二年九月，召拜吏部侍郎。 帝以肅嘗侍太子，言論典正，復令兼太子賓客，為東宮授經。 既而太子失寵，上不悅，有廢斥意。 肅因召見，深陳邦國大本、君臣父子之義。 上改容嘉之。 而太子竟以楊妃故得罪。 乃以肅檢校禮部尚書，兼河中尹、河中節度、晉絳觀察等使。 會昌初，武宗思太子永之無罪，盡誅陷永之黨。 朝議稱肅忠正，有大臣之節。 召拜太常卿，累遷戶部、兵部尚書。
At that time Prince Yong of Lu was in favor, and Emperor Wenzong selected leading scholars for his household. He appointed Yu Jingxiu, vice minister of revenue, as the prince's tutor; Li Jianfang, a director in the ministry of revenue, as chief administrator; and Su, retaining his existing post, as chief secretary. Su thereby won wider notice. The next year, when Prince Lu was made crown prince, Su was given the additional title of drafting counselor in the chancellery. In the ninth year he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, then soon to right vice director of the department of state affairs, with acting charge of the western selection board. Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as defense and observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, with the concurrent title of grand censor. In the ninth month of the second year he was recalled and appointed vice minister of personnel. Because Su had once served the crown prince and his teachings were sound and upright, the emperor again made him guest of the crown prince and assigned him to lecture in the Eastern Palace. Before long the crown prince fell from favor. The emperor was displeased and began contemplating his removal. Su was summoned to audience and spoke at length on the foundations of the realm and the obligations binding ruler and subject, father and son. The emperor's manner changed and he expressed his approval. Yet in the end the crown prince was condemned because of Consort Yang. Su was then made honorary minister of rites, concurrently prefect of the Hezhong capital, military commissioner of Hezhong, and observer of Jin and Jiang. Early in the Huichang reign, Emperor Wuzong recalling Crown Prince Yong's innocence put to death all who had conspired against him. Court opinion held that Su had shown loyalty and integrity worthy of a great minister. He was recalled as director of the court of imperial sacrifices and rose in succession to minister of revenue and minister of war.

五年，以本官同平章事，加中書、門下二侍郎，監修國史，兼尚書右僕射。 素與李德裕親厚。 宣宗即位，德裕罷知政事，肅亦罷相，復為河中節度使。 以疾辭，拜太子太保，卒。 子洎子洎，咸通中累官尚書郎，出為刺史。 洎子仁規、仁表，俱有俊才，文翰高逸。 孫仁規仁規累遷拾遣、補闕、尚書郎、湖州刺史、尚書郎知制誥，正拜中書舍人，卒。 孫仁表仁表擢第後，從杜審權、趙騭為華州、河中掌書記，入為起居郎。 仁表文章尤稱俊拔，然恃才傲物，人士薄之。 自謂門地、人物、文章具美，嘗曰：「天瑞有五色雲，人瑞有鄭仁表。 」劉鄴少時，投文於洎，仁表兄弟嗤鄙之。 咸通末，鄴為宰相，仁表竟貶死南荒。 盧商盧商，字為臣，范陽人。 祖昂，灃州刺史。 父廣，河南縣尉。 商，擢進士第，又書判拔萃登科。 少孤貧力學，釋褐秘書省校書郎。 範傅式廉察宣歙，辟為從事。 王播、段文昌相繼鎮西蜀，商皆佐職為記室，累改禮部員外郎。 入朝為工部員外郎、河南縣令，歷工部、度支、司封三郎中。 ，改京兆少尹，權大理卿事。
In the fifth year he was made co-chancellor while retaining his existing post, with additional appointments as vice director of both the secretariat and the chancellery, supervisor of the national history, and right vice director of the department of state affairs. He had long been close to Li Deyu. When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, Deyu was removed from power and Su was also dismissed from the chancellorship, returning to his post as military commissioner of Hezhong. He resigned citing illness, was named grand preceptor of the crown prince, and died. His son Ji—during the Xiantong reign Ji rose through a series of posts to director in the department of state affairs, then served as a prefect. Ji's sons Rengui and Renbiao were both gifted writers whose prose was elegant and distinguished. His grandson Rengui rose through remonstrance officer, supplementation censor, and director in the department of state affairs to prefect of Huzhou, then returned as a drafting director before being formally appointed secretariat drafter; he died in office. His grandson Renbiao, after passing the examinations, served as chief secretary under Du Shenquan and Zhao Zhi in Huazhou and Hezhong, then entered court as palace diarist. Renbiao's writing was admired as especially brilliant, but he flaunted his talent and treated others with contempt, and men of standing held him in low regard. He considered his lineage, character, and literary gifts without equal, and once declared, "When heaven sends an omen it is a five-colored cloud; when earth sends one it is Zheng Renbiao. " In his youth Liu Ye submitted a literary work to Ji, and the Renbiao brothers sneered at it. Near the end of the Xiantong reign Liu Ye became chancellor, and Renbiao was ultimately banished and died in the southern frontier. Lu Shang—whose courtesy name was Weichen—came from Fanyang. His grandfather Ang had been prefect of Fengzhou. His father Guang had served as magistrate of Henan county. Shang passed the jinshi examination and also distinguished himself in the document-judgment examination. Orphaned and poor in youth, he studied with determination. On entering official service he was appointed collator in the secretariat. When Fan Fushi served as incorrupt investigator of Xuan and She, he recruited Shang as a staff officer. When Wang Bo and then Duan Wenchang served in succession as governors of western Shu, Shang served on each man's staff as secretary. He later rose to assistant director in the ministry of rites. He entered court as assistant director in the ministry of works and magistrate of Henan county, then served in succession as director in the ministries of works, revenue, and enfeoffments. He was then made vice prefect of the capital district and acting director of the court of judicial review.

開成初，出為蘇州刺史。 中謝日，賜金紫之服。
Early in the Kaicheng reign he was posted out as prefect of Suzhou. On the day of his formal audience of thanks he was granted robes of gold and purple.
68
初，郡人苦鹽法太煩，奸吏侵漁。 商至，籍見戶，量所要自售，無定額。 蘇人便之，歲課增倍。 宰相領鹽鐵，以其績上，遷潤州刺史、浙西團練觀察使。 入為刑部侍郎，轉京兆尹。 三年，朝廷用兵上黨，飛挽越太行者，環地六七鎮，以商為戶部侍郎，判度支，兼供軍使，軍用無闕。 逆稹蕩平，加檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。
At first the people of the prefecture suffered under onerous salt regulations and predatory corrupt officials. When Shang arrived he registered households, assessed actual need, and allowed people to buy salt freely without fixed quotas. The people of Suzhou found this a relief, and annual tax revenue doubled. The chancellor in charge of the salt and iron monopoly reported his achievement, and Shang was promoted to prefect of Runzhou and training-and-observation commissioner of western Zhejiang. He was recalled as vice minister of punishments, then transferred to prefect of the capital district. In the third year, when the court waged war at Shangdang and urgent supply lines crossed the Taihang range through six or seven garrison zones, Shang was appointed vice minister of revenue with charge of fiscal affairs and concurrently army-supply commissioner, and military needs were fully met. After the rebel Liu Zhi was defeated and pacified, he was made honorary minister of rites, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East Sichuan.

When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he was recalled as vice minister of war. He was soon made co-chancellor while retaining his post, ennobled as duke of Fanyang commandery with two thousand households, and given the concurrent title of minister of works. Several years later he was made honorary minister of works, posted out as observer of E and Yue circuits, and concurrently given the honorary title of minister of war. He requested relief on grounds of illness and was recalled as minister of revenue. That eighth month he died at Hanyin post station, aged seventy-one.

He had five sons: Zhiyuan, Zhiwei, Zhizong, the monk Lang, and Rao.
71
史臣曰：宗閔、嗣復，承宗室世家之地胄，有文學政事之美名，徊翔清華，出入隆顯。 茍能義以為上，群而不黨，議太平於稷、契之列，致人主於勛、華之盛，遭時得位，誰曰不然？ 而舍披鴻猷，狎茲鼠輩，養虞卿而射利，抗德裕以報仇。 矛盾相攻，幾傾王室，沒身蠻瘴，其利伊何？ 古者，廉、藺解仇，冀全國體，而邀歡釋憾，實亂大倫。 世道銷刓，一至於此！ 崔、魏二丞相，嘉言啟奏，無忝正人。 墀、讓史才，肅之禮學，商之長者，或登三事，或踐六卿，以道始終，夫何不韙。
The historians write: Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu were heirs to an eminent imperial-clan house, famed for literary talent and administrative ability. They moved with ease through the highest offices and rose to the most exalted rank. Had they placed righteousness first, joined together without forming factions, debated the path to lasting peace alongside ministers like Ji and Qi, and guided their emperor toward the greatness of Yao and Shun—given their timing and rank, who would deny they might have done so? Instead they cast aside great statecraft, consorted with petty schemers, sheltered allies for profit like Zhao She nurturing Lord Yuqing, and battled Li Deyu to settle private scores. Their factions clashed until the dynasty itself nearly toppled; they ended their lives in exile among malarial frontier wastes—what did they gain? In antiquity Lian Po and Lin Xiangru set aside their feud to preserve the state—but trading favors to vent grievances in fact upended the bonds of propriety. Moral order had decayed until it came to this! Chief ministers Cui and Wei offered sound counsel in their memorials and lived as upright men without reproach. Chi and Rang had historiographic gifts, Su mastered ritual learning, and Shang was a man of steady virtue. Some reached the highest offices, others served across the six ministries, and each pursued the Way to the end—what fault could be found?
72
贊曰：漢誅鉤黨，魏破疽囊。 何鄧之後，二李三楊。 偷權報怨，任國存亡。 書茲覆轍，敢告巖廊！
The encomium reads: The Han purged the faction cliques; Wei lanced the poisoned boil. After the He and Deng faction came the two Li and three Yang cliques. They seized power to settle scores, heedless of whether the realm survived or fell. I record this repeated folly as a warning to those who govern from the high halls of state.
